sentences.zh: 列傳第六十 自序

translations.literal: Biographies 60: Preface
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 60: Preface

sentences.zh: 昔少暤金天氏有裔子曰昧，為玄冥師，生允格、臺駘。

translations.literal: In antiquity Shaohao, of the Jin Tian clan, had a descendant named Mei who served as master of Xuanming; he begot Yunge and Taidai.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Shaohao of the Jin Tian line had a descendant named Mei, who held the office of Xuanming and fathered Yunge and Taidai.

sentences.zh: 臺駘能業其官，宣汾、洮，障大澤以處太原，帝顓頊嘉之，封諸汾川。

translations.literal: Taidai was able to carry on his office; he opened the Fen and Tao, dammed the great marsh to settle Taiyuan; Emperor Zhuanxu praised him and enfeoffed him in the Fen valley.
translations.idiomatic: Taidai succeeded in his father's charge: he dredged the Fen and Tao, blocked the great marsh to establish Taiyuan, and when Emperor Zhuanxu commended him, he was granted fiefs along the Fen.

sentences.zh: 其後四國，沈、姒、蓐、黃。

translations.literal: Afterward there were four states: Shen, Si, Ru, and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants founded four states: Shen, Si, Ru, and Huang.

sentences.zh: 沈子國，今汝南平輿沈亭是也。

translations.literal: The state of the Lord of Shen is the present Shen Pavilion in Pingyu, Runan.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Shenzi lay where Shen Pavilion in Pingyu, Runan, stands today.

sentences.zh: 春秋之時，列於盟會。

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn period it was ranked among the covenant assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: During the Spring and Autumn era it took its place among the states at the great alliances.

sentences.zh: 定公四年，諸侯會召陵伐楚，沈子不會，晉使蔡伐沈，滅之，以沈子嘉歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Duke Ding the feudal lords met at Zhaoling to attack Chu; the Lord of Shen did not attend, and Jin sent Cai to attack Shen, destroyed it, and took Lord Shen Jia captive.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Ding's fourth year the lords assembled at Zhaoling to campaign against Chu. When the ruler of Shen failed to appear, Jin dispatched Cai against Shen, extinguished the state, and carried Lord Jia away as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 其後，因國為氏。

translations.literal: Afterward they took the state name as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the clan adopted Shen as its surname from the fallen state.

sentences.zh: 自茲以降，譜牒罔存。

translations.literal: From that time downward no genealogical registers survive.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, no family registers have been preserved.

sentences.zh: 秦末有沈逞，徵丞相，不就。

translations.literal: At the end of Qin there was Shen Cheng, summoned as Chancellor; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Near the fall of Qin a Shen Cheng was summoned to serve as Chancellor but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 漢初逞曾孫保，封竹邑侯。

translations.literal: In early Han, Cheng's great-grandson Bao was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Han dynasty Cheng's great-grandson Bao was made Marquis of Zhuyi.

sentences.zh: 保子遵，自本國遷居九江之壽春，官至齊王太傅、敷德侯。

translations.literal: Bao's son Zun moved from his native state to Shouchun in Jiujiang; he rose to Grand Tutor of the King of Qi and Marquis of Fude.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's son Zun left their ancestral territory and settled at Shouchun in Jiujiang, eventually serving as Grand Tutor to the King of Qi and holding the title Marquis of Fude.

sentences.zh: 遵子達，驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Zun's son Da was General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zun's son Da became General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 達子乾，尚書令。

translations.literal: Da's son Qian was Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Da's son Qian served as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 乾子弘，南陽太守。

translations.literal: Qian's son Hong was Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Hong was Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 弘子勖，河內守。

translations.literal: Hong's son Xu was Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Xu governed Henei.

sentences.zh: 勖子奮，御史中丞。

translations.literal: Xu's son Fen was Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Fen rose to Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 奮子恪，將作大匠。

translations.literal: Fen's son Ke was Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Fen's son Ke served as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 恪子謙，尚書、關內侯。

translations.literal: Ke's son Qian was Master of Writing and Marquis within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ke's son Qian held office as Master of Writing and was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 謙子靖，濟陰太守。

translations.literal: Qian's son Jing was Administrator of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's son Jing was Administrator of Jiyin.

sentences.zh: 靖子戎，字威卿，仕州為從事，說降劇賊尹良，漢光武嘉其功，封為海昏縣侯，辭不受。

translations.literal: Jing's son Rong, styled Weiqing, served the province as an aide; he persuaded the fierce bandit Yin Liang to submit, and Emperor Guangwu of Han commended his merit and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Haihun county, but he declined to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Rong, courtesy name Weiqing, served as a provincial aide and talked the rebel Yin Liang into surrender. Emperor Guangwu rewarded him with a marquisate at Haihun, but Rong refused the title.

sentences.zh: 因避地徙居會稽烏程縣之餘不鄉，遂世家焉。

translations.literal: Because he sought refuge from turmoil he moved to Yubu township in Wucheng county, Kuaiji, and his family settled there for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the chaos, he relocated to Yubu in Wucheng, Kuaiji, and the clan made its home there for generations.

sentences.zh: 順帝永建元年，分會稽為吳郡，復為吳郡人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongjian of Emperor Shun, Kuaiji was divided and Wu commandery established; they again became people of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 1 of Emperor Shun, when Kuaiji was split and Wu commandery created, the family became subjects of Wu.

sentences.zh: 靈帝初平五年，分烏程、餘杭為永安縣，吳孫皓寶鼎二年，分吳郡為吳興郡，復為郡人，雖邦邑屢改，而築室不遷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chuping of Emperor Ling, Wucheng and Yuhang were separated as Yong'an county; in the second year of Baoding of Sun Hao of Wu, Wu commandery was divided into Wuxing commandery, and they again became people of the commandery; although the district changed repeatedly, their dwelling was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuping 5 of Emperor Ling, Wucheng and Yuhang were carved out as Yong'an county; in Baoding 2 of Sun Hao of Wu, Wu commandery became Wuxing commandery, and the clan was reckoned among its people. Though administrative boundaries shifted again and again, the family house never moved.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝平吳後，太康二年，改永安為武康縣，史臣七世祖延始居縣東鄉之博陸里餘烏村。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wu of Jin pacified Wu, in the second year of Taikang Yong'an was renamed Wukang county; the historian's seventh-generation ancestor Yan first dwelt at Yuwu village in Bolu township, eastern district of the county.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin Emperor Wu conquered Wu, Yong'an was renamed Wukang in Taikang 2. The historian's seventh-generation forebear Yan first settled at Yuwu in Bolu, in the county's eastern township.

sentences.zh: 王父從官京師，義熙十一年，高祖賜館于建康都亭里之運巷。

translations.literal: The historian's grandfather followed office to the capital; in the eleventh year of Yixi the High Ancestor granted a residence in Yun lane, Duting ward, Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's grandfather followed his post to the capital, and in Yixi 11 the High Ancestor granted the family a house in Yun Lane, Duting Ward, Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 戎子酆，字聖通，零陵太守，致黃龍、芝草之瑞。

translations.literal: Rong's son Feng, styled Shengtong, was Administrator of Lingling and brought about auspicious signs of yellow dragons and spirit fungus.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's son Feng, courtesy name Shengtong, governed Lingling and was credited with prodigies of yellow dragons and sacred fungus.

sentences.zh: 第二子滸，字仲高，安平相。

translations.literal: The second son Hu, styled Zhonggao, was Chancellor of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Hu, courtesy name Zhonggao, served as Chancellor of Anping.

sentences.zh: 少子景，河間相，演之、慶之、曇慶、懷文其後也。

translations.literal: The youngest son Jing was Chancellor of Hejian; Yanzhi, Qingzhi, Tanqing, and Huaiwen were his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Jing was Chancellor of Hejian; from his line came Yanzhi, Qingzhi, Tanqing, and Huaiwen.

sentences.zh: 滸子鸞，字建光，少有高名，州舉茂才，公府辟州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: Hu's son Luan, styled Jianguang, had a lofty reputation in youth; the province recommended him as Prominent Talent, and the government office summoned him as Attendant Clerk to the Commandery Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's son Luan, courtesy name Jianguang, won early renown; the province nominated him as Prominent Talent, and the central offices appointed him Attendant Clerk to the Commandery Aide.

sentences.zh: 時廣陵太守陸稠，鸞之舅也，以義烈政績，顯名漢朝，復以女妻鸞。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Chou, Administrator of Guangling, was Luan's maternal uncle; for righteous valor and administrative achievement he was illustrious in the Han court, and he again gave his daughter to Luan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou of Guangling, Luan's uncle by marriage, was famed in Han service for his integrity and achievements, and he gave his daughter to Luan as wife.

sentences.zh: 年二十三，早卒。

translations.literal: At age twenty-three he died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young at twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 子直，字伯平，州舉茂才，亦有清名，年二十八卒。

translations.literal: His son Zhi, styled Boping, was recommended by the province as Prominent Talent and also had a pure reputation; he died at twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi, courtesy name Boping, was likewise nominated as Prominent Talent and enjoyed a spotless reputation, but died at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子儀，字仲則，少有至行，兄瑜十歲，儀九歲而父亡，居喪過禮，毀瘠過於成人。

translations.literal: His son Yi, styled Zhongze, had supreme conduct in youth; his elder brother Yu was ten and Yi nine when their father died; in mourning he exceeded the rites and his emaciation surpassed that of adults.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi, courtesy name Zhongze, showed extraordinary filial devotion as a boy. When their father died, Yu was ten and Yi nine; Yi observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites and wasted away more severely than a grown man.

sentences.zh: 外祖會稽盛孝章，漢末名士也，深加憂傷，每擾慰之，曰：「汝並黃中沖爽，終成奇器，何為逾制，自取殄滅邪！

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather Sheng Xiaozhang of Kuaiji was a famous scholar of late Han; deeply grieved, he repeatedly came to comfort him, saying: "You are both pure talent in the prime of youth and will surely become extraordinary vessels—why exceed the regulations and bring ruin on yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng Xiaozhang of Kuaiji, a celebrated scholar of the Han collapse, was deeply alarmed and often came to console him, saying, "You boys are gifted and bright—you will surely become men of mark. Why break the mourning code and destroy yourselves?"

sentences.zh: 」三年禮畢，殆至滅性，故兄弟並以孝著。

translations.literal: When the three-year rites were complete he nearly perished in body, and therefore the brothers were both noted for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the three-year mourning ended he had nearly ruined his health, and both brothers became renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 瑜早卒。

translations.literal: Yu died young.
translations.idiomatic: Yu died young.

sentences.zh: 儀篤學有雄才，以儒素自業。

translations.literal: Yi studied earnestly and had heroic talent, taking Confucian plainness as his profession.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a devoted scholar of formidable ability who devoted himself to the plain Confucian way.

sentences.zh: 時海內大亂，兵革並起，經術道弛，士少全行，而儀淳深隱默，守道不移，風操貞整，不妄交納，唯與族子仲山、叔山及吳郡陸公紀友善。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was in great disorder, arms arose everywhere, the way of classical learning was relaxed, and few scholars preserved their conduct intact; yet Yi was pure, deep, and reticent, holding the Way without shifting, his bearing upright and whole, not making acquaintances rashly—he was friendly only with his clansmen Zhongshan and Shushan and Lu Gongji of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: While the empire convulsed in war and learning decayed, few men kept their integrity—but Yi remained grave, silent, and steadfast, his conduct unblemished and his friendships few: only his kinsmen Zhongshan and Shushan, and Lu Gongji of Wu.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮請，二府交辟，公車徵，並不屈，以壽終。

translations.literal: The province and commanderies invited him with ceremony; both offices jointly summoned him; the imperial carriage summoned him—all he refused, and he ended his life in full years.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery offices courted him; both central bureaus and the imperial summons reached him—he declined them all and lived out his years at home.

sentences.zh: 子憲，字元禮，左中郎、新都都尉、定陽侯，才志顯于吳朝。

translations.literal: His son Xian, styled Yuanli, was Left Gentleman-of-the-Palace, Commandant of Xindu, and Marquis of Dingyang; his talent and resolve were illustrious in the Wu court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian, courtesy name Yuanli, served Wu as Left Gentleman-of-the-Palace, Commandant of Xindu, and Marquis of Dingyang, and his ability and ambition were well known at court.

sentences.zh: 子矯，字仲桓，以節氣立名，仕為立武校尉、偏將軍，封列侯，建威將軍、新都太守。

translations.literal: His son Jiao, styled Zhonghuan, established his name through integrity and spirit; he served as Colonel of Established Martiality, General of the Left, was enfeoffed as a ranked marquis, and was General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao, courtesy name Zhonghuan, won fame for his fortitude, rising to Colonel of Established Martiality and General of the Left, enfeoffed as a full marquis, and finally General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 孫皓時，有將帥之稱。

translations.literal: Under Sun Hao he had the reputation of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Hao he was accounted a leading general.

sentences.zh: 吳平後，為鬱林、長沙太守，並不就。

translations.literal: After Wu was pacified he was made Administrator of Yulin and Changsha but did not take either post.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Wu he was offered Yulin and Changsha but refused both appointments.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒。

translations.literal: He died at the end of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Taikang era.

sentences.zh: 子陵，字景高，太傅東海王越辟為從事。

translations.literal: His son Ling, styled Jinggao, was summoned as an aide by the Grand Tutor, Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ling, courtesy name Jinggao, was recruited as an aide by Grand Tutor Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 元帝之為鎮東將軍，命參軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan was General Who Guards the East, he appointed Ling a military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Yuan served as General Who Guards the East, he made Ling his military adviser.

sentences.zh: 徐馥作亂，殺吳興太守袁琇，陵討平之。

translations.literal: Xu Fu rebelled and killed Yuan Xiu, Administrator of Wuxing; Ling suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Fu rebelled and killed Yuan Xiu, Administrator of Wuxing, Ling crushed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 子延，字思長，桓溫安西參軍、潁川太守。

translations.literal: His son Yan, styled Sichang, was a military adviser to Huan Wen's Anxi headquarters and Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, courtesy name Sichang, served Huan Wen's western headquarters and governed Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 子賀，字子寧，桓沖南中郎參軍，圍袁真于壽陽，遇疾卒。

translations.literal: His son He, styled Zining, was military adviser to Huan Chong's Southern Palace Gentleman headquarters; besieging Yuan Zhen at Shouyang, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son He, courtesy name Zining, was an adviser in Huan Chong's southern command; while besieging Yuan Zhen at Shouyang he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 子警，字世明，惇篤有行業，學通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: His son Jing, styled Shiming, was sincere and steadfast with established conduct, and mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jing, courtesy name Shiming, was a man of sincere character and solid achievement who mastered the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 家世富殖，財產累千金，仕郡主簿，後將軍謝安命為參軍，甚相敬重。

translations.literal: His family had been wealthy for generations, with property amounting to thousands in gold; he served as chief clerk of the commandery, and General of the Rear Xie An appointed him military adviser and greatly respected him.
translations.idiomatic: The family had long been wealthy, with estates worth thousands in gold. Jing served as a commandery chief clerk until General of the Rear Xie An made him his adviser and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 警內足於財，為東南豪士，無仕進意，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Jing was inwardly sufficient in wealth, a magnate of the southeast, and had no wish to advance in office; he pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Content with his wealth and ranked among the great men of the southeast, Jing had no ambition for further office and resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 安固留不止，乃謂警曰：「沈參軍，卿有獨善之志，不亦高乎！

translations.literal: An firmly detained him and would not let him go, then said to Jing: "Military Adviser Shen, you have the will to cultivate yourself alone—is that not lofty!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie An pressed him to stay, then said, "Adviser Shen, your wish to perfect yourself in private life—is that not admirable!"

sentences.zh: 」警曰：「使君以道御物，前所以懷德而至，既無用佐時，故遂飲啄之願爾。

translations.literal: Jing said: "My lord governs affairs by the Way; that is why I came before in gratitude for your virtue. Since I am of no use in aiding the age, I therefore fulfill the wish merely to drink and peck as nature allows."
translations.idiomatic: Jing replied, "You govern by the Way—that is why I came to you in the first place. Finding I can be of no service to the times, I mean only to live out my days in quiet contentment."

sentences.zh: 」還家積載，以素業自娛。

translations.literal: He returned home with accumulated stores and amused himself with plain pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to his estates and devoted himself to a simple life.

sentences.zh: 前將軍、青、兗二州刺史王恭鎮京口，與警有舊好，復引為參軍，手書殷勤，苦相招致，不得已而應之，尋復謝職。

translations.literal: General of the Van Wang Gong, Governor of Qing and Yan provinces, garrisoned Jingkou and had an old friendship with Jing; he again recruited him as military adviser, writing by his own hand with earnest courtesy and pressing him hard to come—unable to refuse, Jing assented, but soon resigned again.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong, General of the Van and governor of Qing and Yan, held Jingkou and renewed their old friendship by appointing Jing his adviser. Wang's own letter was warm and insistent; Jing yielded reluctantly but soon resigned once more.

sentences.zh: 子穆夫，字彥和，少好學，亦通《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: His son Mufu, styled Yanhe, loved learning in youth and also mastered the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mufu, courtesy name Yanhe, was a devoted student in youth and likewise mastered the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 王恭命為前軍主簿，與警書曰：「足下既執不拔之志，高臥東南，故屈賢子共事，非以吏職嬰之也。

translations.literal: Wang Gong appointed him chief clerk of the Forward Army and wrote to Jing: "You, sir, hold an unyielding will and recline loftily in the southeast; therefore I have bent your worthy son to serve with me—not to bind him with an official post."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong made him chief clerk of the Forward Army and wrote to Jing, "You hold firm to your resolve and live in retirement in the southeast; I ask only that your worthy son work with me—not to trap him in office."

sentences.zh: 」初，錢唐人杜子恭通靈有道術，東土豪家及京邑貴望，並事之為弟子，執在三之敬。

translations.literal: Earlier, Du Zigong of Qiantang had communion with spirits and possessed the Way and its arts; great families of the eastern lands and eminent nobles of the capital all served him as disciples, observing the reverence due to father, elder brother, and teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Du Zigong of Qiantang was famed for spirit-medium powers and Daoist arts; wealthy eastern families and great men of the capital all became his disciples and showed him the triple reverence owed to father, elder brother, and teacher.

sentences.zh: 警累世事道，亦敬事子恭。

translations.literal: Jing's family for generations served the Way and also reverently served Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had followed the Way, and Jing too honored Du Zigong.

sentences.zh: 子恭死，門徒孫泰、泰弟子恩傳其業，警復事之。

translations.literal: When Zigong died, his disciple Sun Tai and Tai's disciple En transmitted his teaching; Jing again served them.
translations.idiomatic: After Zigong's death his disciple Sun Tai, and Tai's disciple Sun En, carried on his teaching; Jing served them in turn.

sentences.zh: 隆安三年，恩於會稽作亂，自稱征東將軍，三吳皆響應。

translations.literal: In the third year of Long'an, En rebelled in Kuaiji, styled himself General Who Conquers the East, and the Three Wu regions all responded.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an 3 Sun En rose in Kuaiji, proclaimed himself General Who Conquers the East, and the Three Wu districts rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 穆夫時在會稽，恩以為前部參軍、振武將軍、餘姚令。

translations.literal: Mufu was then in Kuaiji; En made him Forward Army military adviser, General Who Quells Martiality, and Magistrate of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Mufu was in Kuaiji at the time; En appointed him Forward Army adviser, General Who Quells Martiality, and magistrate of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月二十八日，恩為劉牢之所破，輔國將軍高素於山陰回踵埭執穆夫及偽吳郡太守陸瑰之、吳興太守丘尪，並見害，函首送京邑，事見《隆安故事》。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month of that year En was defeated by Liu Laozhi; Auxiliary General Gao Su at Huizhong dam in Shanyin seized Mufu and the false Administrators of Wu commandery Lu Guizhi and of Wuxing Qiu Kuang; all were killed, their heads boxed and sent to the capital—the affair is recorded in the Long'an Annals.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth of the twelfth month En was routed by Liu Laozhi. At Huizhong Dam in Shanyin, Auxiliary General Gao Su captured Mufu along with the rebel administrators Lu Guizhi of Wu and Qiu Kuang of Wuxing; all were executed and their heads sent to the capital, as recorded in the Long'an Annals.

sentences.zh: 先是，宗人沈預素無士行，為警所疾，至是警聞穆夫預亂，逃藏將免矣，預以告官，警及穆夫、弟仲夫、任夫、預夫、佩夫並遇害；

translations.literal: Earlier, the clansman Shen Yu had never had the conduct of a gentleman and was disliked by Jing; when Jing heard that Mufu had joined the rebellion he fled into hiding and was about to escape, but Yu informed the authorities; Jing and Mufu and his brothers Zhongfu, Renfu, Yufu, and Peifu were all killed;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the kinsman Shen Yu, a man of poor character whom Jing despised, learned that Mufu had joined the rebellion. Jing went into hiding and was near escape, but Yu informed the authorities. Jing, Mufu, and the brothers Zhongfu, Renfu, Yufu, and Peifu were all put to death;

sentences.zh: 唯穆夫子淵子、雲子、田子、林子、虔子獲全。

translations.literal: only Mufu's sons Yuanzi, Yunzi, Tianzi, Linzi, and Qianzi were spared.
translations.idiomatic: only Mufu's sons Yuanzi, Yunzi, Tianzi, Linzi, and Qianzi survived.

sentences.zh: 淵子，字敬深，少有志節，隨高祖克京城，封繁畤縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Yuanzi, styled Jingshen, had resolve and integrity in youth; following the High Ancestor in capturing the capital region he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Fanzhi county.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzi, courtesy name Jingshen, showed early fortitude and merit; he followed the High Ancestor in the capture of the capital and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 參鎮軍、車騎中軍事，又為道規輔國、征西參軍，領寧蜀太守。

translations.literal: He served on the staffs of the Pacifying Army and the Chariots and Cavalry as central army aide, and again as military adviser to Daogui's Pacifying Army and Western Campaign headquarters, concurrently holding the post of Administrator of Ningshu.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staffs of the Pacifying Army and the Chariots and Cavalry, then as adviser to Daogui's western command while governing Ningshu.

sentences.zh: 與劉基共斬蔡猛於大簿，還為太尉參軍，從征司馬休之，與徐逵之同沒。

translations.literal: With Liu Ji he jointly beheaded Cai Meng at Dabo; he returned to serve as military adviser to the Grand Marshal, followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, and perished together with Xu Daizhi.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Ji he slew Cai Meng at Dabo, then served as adviser to the Grand Marshal on the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, where he fell alongside Xu Daizhi.

sentences.zh: 時年三十五。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-five years old.

sentences.zh: 子正，字元直，淹詳有器度，美風姿，善容止，好老、莊之學。

translations.literal: His son Zheng, styled Yuanzhi, was broad and thorough with great capacity; he had a fine bearing, graceful deportment, and loved the learning of Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng, courtesy name Yuanzhi, was learned, broad-minded, and handsome in bearing, with graceful manners and a devotion to Laozi and Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州辟從事。

translations.literal: At capping age the province summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was recruited as a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 宗人光祿大夫演之稱之曰：「此宗中千里駒也。

translations.literal: His clansman Yanzhi, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, praised him, saying: "This is the thousand-li colt of our clan."
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yanzhi, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, called him "the thousand-li steed of our clan."

sentences.zh: 」出為始寧、烏傷、婁令，母憂去職。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as magistrate of Shining, Wushang, and Lou; on his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shining, Wushang, and Lou in turn, then resigned on his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為隨王誕後軍安南行參軍。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he became mobile military adviser on the Rear Army Pacify-the-South staff of Prince of Sui, Dan.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he joined Prince Dan of Sui's Rear Army Pacify-the-South staff as mobile adviser.

sentences.zh: 誕鎮會稽，復參安東軍事。

translations.literal: When Dan garrisoned Kuaiji, Zheng again served on the Pacify-the-East military staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan took up his post at Kuaiji, Zheng again served on his Pacify-the-East staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年，元兇弑立，分江東為會州，以誕為刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia the Crown Prince assassin seized the throne; the lands east of the Yangzi were divided into Huizhou, and Dan was made its governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 30, after the crown prince's regicide, the eastern Yangzi region was made into Huizhou and Dan was appointed its governor.

sentences.zh: 誕將受命，正說司馬顧琛曰：「國家此禍，開闢未聞，今以江東義銳之眾，為天下倡始，若馳一介，四方詎不回應。

translations.literal: As Dan was about to accept the commission, Zheng persuaded Chief Administrator Gu Chen: "This calamity of the state is unheard of since the world's beginning; now with the righteous and sharp hosts of the eastern Yangzi, take the lead for all under Heaven—if you send a single envoy, how could the four quarters fail to respond!"
translations.idiomatic: As Dan prepared to accept office, Zheng urged Chief Administrator Gu Chen, "A crime unheard of since the founding of the realm—yet with the loyal armies of the east we could lead the empire. Send one messenger abroad and who would not answer?"

sentences.zh: 以此雪朝庭冤恥，大明臣子之節，豈可北面凶逆，使殿下受其偽寵。

translations.literal: By this avenge the court's wrong and shame, make bright the integrity of subject and minister—how can you turn north to the murderous rebel and let Your Highness receive his false favor!
translations.idiomatic: Thus we would wipe away the court's disgrace and show what loyalty means. How can you bow to a regicide and let Your Highness accept favors from a usurper?

sentences.zh: 」琛曰：「江東忘戰日久，士不習兵。

translations.literal: Chen said: "The eastern Yangzi has long forgotten war; the warriors are unpracticed in arms."
translations.idiomatic: Chen replied, "The east has known peace too long; our men are unused to war."

sentences.zh: 雖云逆順不同，然強弱又異，當須四方有義舉者，然後應之，不為晚也。

translations.literal: Although one may say right and wrong differ, yet strong and weak also differ; we must wait until the four quarters have righteous uprisings, and then respond—it will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Right may differ from wrong, but strength differs too. We should wait until righteous armies rise elsewhere, then join them—it will not be too late.

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「天下若有無父之國，則可矣。

translations.literal: Zheng said: "If there were a realm without fathers under Heaven, that would do."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Only if there were an empire without fathers could we wait."

sentences.zh: 苟其不爾，寧可自安仇恥，而責義於餘方。

translations.literal: If it is not so, how can one rest secure in hatred and shame while demanding righteousness from other regions!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise how can we rest easy in our shame while demanding virtue from others?

sentences.zh: 今正以弑逆冤醜，義不同戴，舉兵之日，豈求必全耶！

translations.literal: Now precisely because of the regicide's grievous shame, righteousness cannot share the same canopy with him—on the day arms are raised, who seeks certain preservation!
translations.idiomatic: The regicide's crime forbids us to live under the same sky. When we take up arms, who expects to survive unscathed?

sentences.zh: 馮衍有言，大漢之貴臣，將不如荊、齊之賤士乎！

translations.literal: Feng Yan said: shall the noble ministers of great Han be inferior to the mean knights of Jing and Qi!
translations.idiomatic: As Feng Yan asked, shall great Han's nobles prove less valiant than the humble men of Jing and Qi?

sentences.zh: 況殿下義兼臣子，事實家國者哉！

translations.literal: How much more when Your Highness's righteousness embraces both subject and son, and the affair is in truth the family and the state!
translations.idiomatic: And you, my lord, owe duty both as prince and as subject—the realm and the house are one!

sentences.zh: 」琛乃與正俱入說誕，誕猶預未決。

translations.literal: Chen then entered with Zheng together to persuade Dan, but Dan still hesitated and had not decided.
translations.idiomatic: Chen went in with Zheng to persuade Dan, but Dan still wavered.

sentences.zh: 會尋陽義兵起，世祖使至，誕乃加正寧朔將軍，領軍繼劉季之。

translations.literal: Just then righteous troops rose at Xunyang and an envoy of Emperor Shizu arrived; Dan thereupon promoted Zheng to General Who Pacifies the North and had the army follow Liu Jizhi.
translations.idiomatic: When loyal forces rose at Xunyang and an envoy from the future Emperor Shizu arrived, Dan made Zheng General Who Pacifies the North and put him in command after Liu Jizhi.

sentences.zh: 誕入為驃騎大將軍，正為中兵參軍，遷長水校尉。

translations.literal: When Dan entered the capital as General of Agile Cavalry, Zheng became central army military adviser and was transferred to Colonel of the Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan entered the capital as General of Agile Cavalry, Zheng served as central army adviser and was promoted to Colonel of the Changshui.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，移青州鎮歷城，臨淄地空，除寧朔將軍、齊、北海二郡太守，委以全齊之任。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian the Qingzhou garrison was moved to Licheng; the Linzi region lay empty; Zheng was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Qi and Beihai, entrusted with the task of securing all Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian 1 the Qingzhou garrison moved to Licheng with Linzi left undefended; Zheng was made General Who Pacifies the North and dual administrator of Qi and Beihai, charged with holding all of Qi.

sentences.zh: 未拜，二年卒，時年四十三。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the appointment, in the second year he died, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post he died in the second year, at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 正生好樂，厚自奉養，既終之後，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Zheng loved music in life and indulged himself richly; after his death the family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng loved music and lived generously; when he died the family was left with nothing.

sentences.zh: 淵子弟雲子，元嘉中，為晉安太守。

translations.literal: Yuanzi's younger brother Yunzi, in the Yuanjia era, was Administrator of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzi's younger brother Yunzi served as Administrator of Jin'an during the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 雲子子煥，字士蔚，少為駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: Yunzi's son Huan, styled Shiwei, in youth was Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law and Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: Yunzi's son Huan, courtesy name Shiwei, early held the posts of Commandant of the Horse Guards for the Emperor's Sons-in-Law and Attendant at Court.

sentences.zh: 元兇之入弑也，煥時兼中庶子，直坊，逼從入臺。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince assassin entered to commit regicide, Huan was concurrently Junior Tutor and on duty in the side palace; he was forced to follow into the inner platform.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince carried out the regicide, Huan was serving as Junior Tutor on palace duty and was compelled to follow him into the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 劭既自立，以為羽林監，辭不拜，拜員外散騎侍郎，使防南譙王義宣諸子，事在《義宣傳》。

translations.literal: After Shao had established himself he appointed Huan Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers; Huan declined to accept and was appointed Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier; he was sent to guard the sons of the Prince of Nanqiao, Yixuan—the affair is in the Biography of Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shao seized the throne he offered Huan the post of Supervisor of the Forest of Feathers; Huan refused and was made Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier, then assigned to guard the sons of Prince Yixuan of Nanqiao, as told in Yixuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 仍除丞相行參軍，員外散騎侍郎，南昌令，有能名。

translations.literal: He was then appointed mobile military adviser to the Chancellor, Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier, and Magistrate of Nanchang, and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made mobile adviser to the Chancellor, Extraordinary Attendant Cavalier, and magistrate of Nanchang, winning a name for competence.

sentences.zh: 晉平王休祐驃騎中兵記室參軍，同僚皆以諂進，煥獨不。

translations.literal: Under Prince of Jinping Xiuyou he was recording secretary on the central army staff of the General of Agile Cavalry; his colleagues all advanced by flattery, but Huan alone did not.
translations.idiomatic: Under Prince Xiuyou of Jinping he served as recording secretary on the General of Agile Cavalry's staff; while his colleagues curried favor, Huan alone would not.

sentences.zh: 頃之，記室參軍周敬祖等為太宗所責得罪，轉煥諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Before long the recording secretaries Zhou Jingzu and others were blamed and punished by Emperor Taizong; Huan was transferred to advisory military adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward recording secretaries including Zhou Jingzu were punished on Emperor Taizong's orders; Huan was transferred to advisory military adviser.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽中，以為寧遠將軍、交州刺史，未至鎮，病卒，時年四十五。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era of the deposed emperor he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Jiaozhou; before reaching his post he died of illness, aged forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Houfei's Yuanhui reign he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and governor of Jiaozhou, but fell ill and died before taking up the post, at forty-five.

sentences.zh: 田子，字敬光，雲子弟也。

translations.literal: Tianzi, styled Jingguang, was Yunzi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi, courtesy name Jingguang, was Yunzi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 從高祖克京城，進平京邑，參鎮軍軍事，封營道縣五等侯。

translations.literal: He followed the High Ancestor in capturing the capital region, advanced to pacify the capital city, served on the Pacifying Army staff, and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Yingdao county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the High Ancestor in the capture of the capital and its pacification, joined the Pacifying Army staff, and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Yingdao.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，高祖北伐鮮卑。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi the High Ancestor marched north against the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 5 the High Ancestor launched his northern campaign against the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 田子領偏師，與龍驤將軍孟龍符為前鋒。

translations.literal: Tianzi led a detached force and with General of Agile Cavalry Meng Longfu served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi commanded a detached column and, with General of Agile Cavalry Meng Longfu, led the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 慕容超屯臨朐以距大軍，龍符戰沒，田子力戰破之。

translations.literal: Murong Chao encamped at Linqu to block the great army; Longfu fell in battle, but Tianzi fought fiercely and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao held Linqu against the main army. Longfu was killed in battle, but Tianzi fought hard and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及盧循逼京邑，高祖遣田子與建威將軍孫季高由海道襲廣州，加振武將軍。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital region, the High Ancestor sent Tianzi with General Who Establishes Might Sun Jigao by sea to strike Guangzhou, and promoted Tianzi to General Who Quells Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, the High Ancestor sent Tianzi with Sun Jigao, General Who Establishes Might, by sea against Guangzhou and promoted Tianzi to General Who Quells Martiality.

sentences.zh: 循黨徐道覆還保始興，田子復與右將軍劉藩同共攻討。

translations.literal: Xun's partisan Xu Daofu withdrew to defend Shixing; Tianzi again joined General of the Right Liu Fan in joint attack and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's lieutenant Xu Daofu fell back to defend Shixing, and Tianzi again campaigned alongside General of the Right Liu Fan.

sentences.zh: 循尋還廣州圍季高，田子慮季高孤危，謂藩曰：「廣州城雖險固，本是賊之巢穴。

translations.literal: Before long Xun returned to Guangzhou to besiege Jigao; Tianzi feared Jigao was isolated and in peril, and said to Fan: "Though Guangzhou's walls are strong, it was originally the rebels' lair."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xun returned to besiege Jigao at Guangzhou. Tianzi feared for his isolated comrade and told Fan, "Guangzhou may be strong, but it was the rebels' own stronghold."

sentences.zh: 今循還圍之，或有內變。

translations.literal: Now that Xun has returned to besiege it, there may be internal unrest.
translations.idiomatic: With Xun back to invest it, there may be treachery within the walls.

sentences.zh: 且季高眾力寡弱，不能持久。

translations.literal: Moreover Jigao's forces are few and weak and cannot hold out long.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Jigao's men are few and weak—they cannot last.

sentences.zh: 若使賊還據此，凶勢復振。

translations.literal: If the rebels regain this place, their fierce power will revive.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels hold it again, their power will revive.

sentences.zh: 下官與季高同履艱難，泛滄海，於萬死之中，克平廣州，豈可坐視危逼，不相拯救。

translations.literal: Your humble servant and Jigao together endured hardship, crossed the blue sea, and amid ten thousand deaths conquered Guangzhou—how can we sit and watch him pressed to peril without going to his aid!
translations.idiomatic: Jigao and I crossed the sea together and took Guangzhou at the risk of our lives. How can we stand by while he is cornered?

sentences.zh: 」於是率軍南還，比至，賊已收其散卒，還圍廣州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the army southward in return; by the time he arrived the rebels had gathered their scattered troops and again besieged Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south at once, but by the time he arrived the rebels had rallied their scattered forces and renewed the siege of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 季高單守危迫，聞田子忽至，大喜。

translations.literal: Jigao alone held the city in desperate straits; hearing that Tianzi had suddenly arrived, he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao held the city alone in desperate straits and rejoiced when Tianzi appeared.

sentences.zh: 田子乃背水結陳，身率先士卒，一戰破之。

translations.literal: Tianzi then formed battle lines with water at his back, personally led the assault ahead of his soldiers, and in one battle broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi drew up his line with water at his back, led the charge in person, and routed the enemy in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 於是推鋒追討，又破循於蒼梧、鬱林、寧浦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pressed the attack in pursuit and again defeated Xun at Cangwu, Yulin, and Ningpu.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the pursuit and defeated Xun again at Cangwu, Yulin, and Ningpu.

sentences.zh: 還至廣州，而季高病死。

translations.literal: On returning to Guangzhou, Jigao had died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to Guangzhou, Jigao had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 既兵荒之後，山賊競出，攻沒城郭，殺害長吏。

translations.literal: After the war and famine, mountain bandits swarmed forth, attacked and overran walled towns, and killed chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: After the wars and famine, mountain bandits rose everywhere, sacked towns, and killed local officials.

sentences.zh: 田子隨宜討伐，旬日平殄。

translations.literal: Tianzi suppressed them as occasion required and within ten days pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi suppressed them as needed and within ten days had wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 刺史褚升度至，乃還京師。

translations.literal: When Governor Chu Shengdu arrived, he then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Governor Chu Shengdu arrived, Tianzi returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 除太尉參軍、振武將軍、淮陵內史，賜爵都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed military adviser to the Grand Marshal, General Who Quells Martiality, and Interior Minister of Huailing, and granted the title Marquis of the Metropolitan Township.
translations.idiomatic: He was made adviser to the Grand Marshal, General Who Quells Martiality, and interior minister of Huailing, and enfeoffed as Marquis of the Metropolitan Township.

sentences.zh: 復參世子征虜軍事，將軍、內史如故。

translations.literal: He again served on the heir's Pacify-the-Captive staff; his posts as general and interior minister remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the heir's Pacify-the-Captive staff while retaining his rank as general and interior minister.

sentences.zh: 八年，從討劉毅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the campaign against Liu Yi.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復從討司馬休之，領別軍，與征虜將軍趙倫之，參征虜軍事、振武將軍、扶風太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, commanding a detached army with General Who Pacifies the Captive Zhao Lunzhi; he served as military adviser on the Pacify-the-Captive staff, General Who Quells Martiality, and Administrator of Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he campaigned again against Sima Xiuzhi at the head of a detached force with Zhao Lunzhi, General Who Pacifies the Captive, and served as Pacify-the-Captive adviser, General Who Quells Martiality, and administrator of Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖北伐，田子與順陽太守傅弘之各領別軍，從武關入，屯據青泥。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the High Ancestor marched north; Tianzi and Administrator of Shunyang Fu Hongzhi each led detached armies, entered by Wuguan, and encamped at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, on the northern campaign, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi of Shunyang each led detached columns through Wuguan and encamped at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 姚泓欲自御大軍，慮田子襲其後，欲先平田子，然後傾國東出。

translations.literal: Yao Hong wished to face the great army himself but feared Tianzi would strike his rear; he wished first to defeat Tianzi, then move the whole state eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong meant to face the main army but feared an attack from Tianzi in his rear; he resolved to crush Tianzi first, then march east with his full strength.

sentences.zh: 乃率步軍數萬，奄至清泥。

translations.literal: He thereupon led several tens of thousands of infantry and suddenly arrived at Qingni.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with tens of thousands of foot soldiers and suddenly appeared at Qingni.

sentences.zh: 田子本為疑兵，所領裁數百，欲擊之。

translations.literal: Tianzi had originally been a diversionary force and commanded only a few hundred men, yet he wished to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi's detachment was meant only as a diversion—he had but a few hundred men—yet he meant to attack.

sentences.zh: 傅弘之曰：「彼眾我寡，難可與敵。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi said: "They are many and we are few; it will be hard to meet them in battle."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi said, "They outnumber us—we cannot fight them."

sentences.zh: 」田子曰：「師貴用奇，不必在眾。

translations.literal: Tianzi said: "In warfare what matters is the unexpected; numbers are not everything."
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi replied, "Warfare depends on surprise, not numbers alone."

sentences.zh: 」弘之猶固執，田子曰：「眾寡相傾，勢不兩立。

translations.literal: Hongzhi still held firm; Tianzi said: "When many and few confront each other, only one side can stand."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi still objected. Tianzi said, "When forces meet, only one side can survive."

sentences.zh: 若使賊圍既固，人情喪沮，事便去矣。

translations.literal: If the enemy's encirclement is already firm and men's spirits sink in despair, the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If their siege tightens and our men's hearts fail, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 及其未整，薄之必克，所謂先人有奪人之志也。

translations.literal: Strike before they are arrayed and we are sure to prevail—that is what is meant by seizing the enemy's will before he seizes yours.
translations.idiomatic: Attack before they are ready and we shall win—that is seizing the initiative before the enemy takes heart.

sentences.zh: 」便獨率所領鼓而進。

translations.literal: Thereupon he alone led his command forward with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men forward alone, drums rolling.

sentences.zh: 合圍數重，田子撫慰士卒曰：「諸君捐親戚，棄墳墓，出矢石之間，正希今日耳。

translations.literal: The encirclement closed in several rings deep; Tianzi comforted his soldiers, saying: "You gentlemen have left kin and abandoned ancestral graves to stand amid arrows and stones—you have long hoped for this day."
translations.idiomatic: Ring after ring closed around them. Tianzi rallied his men: "You left home and graves to face arrows and stones—you have waited for this day."

sentences.zh: 封侯之業，其在此乎！

translations.literal: The achievement of enfeoffment—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: The marquisate you seek—is it not won today!

sentences.zh: 」乃棄糧毀舍，躬勒士卒，前後奮擊，所向摧陷。

translations.literal: He then cast aside provisions and burned his camp, personally drove his soldiers, charged forward and back with fierce assault, and wherever he turned the enemy was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: He burned his stores and camp, led the charge in person, and wherever he struck the enemy line gave way.

sentences.zh: 所領江東勇士，便習短兵，鼓噪奔之，賊眾一時潰散，所殺萬餘人，得泓偽乘輿服御。

translations.literal: The Jiangdong warriors under his command were skilled with short weapons; with clamor and charge they rushed the foe, and the rebel host collapsed at once; more than ten thousand were killed, and Hong's false imperial carriage and regalia were captured.
translations.idiomatic: His Jiangdong veterans, adept with short weapons, charged with a great clamor; the enemy broke at once. More than ten thousand were slain, and Hong's false imperial regalia was taken.

sentences.zh: 高祖表言曰：「參征虜軍事、振武將軍、扶風太守沈田子，率領勁銳，背城電激，身先士卒，勇冠戎陳，奮寡對眾，所向必摧，自辰及未，斬馘千數。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor memorialized: "Military adviser on the Pacify-the-Captive staff, General Who Quells Martiality, Administrator of Fufeng Shen Tianzi led crack troops, struck like lightning with water at his back, went before his soldiers in person, his courage surpassing all in the battle array; rousing the few against the many, wherever he turned he shattered the foe; from the hour chen to wei he cut down thousands."
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor reported: "Shen Tianzi, Pacify-the-Captive adviser, General Who Quells Martiality, and administrator of Fufeng, led elite troops in a lightning strike with his back to the wall. He surpassed all in courage, drove the few against the many, and broke every line he met. From mid-morning to mid-afternoon he slew thousands."

sentences.zh: 泓喪旗棄眾，奔還霸西，咸陽空盡，義徒四合，清蕩餘燼，勢在跂踵。

translations.literal: Hong abandoned his banners and cast off his troops, fleeing back to Baxia; Xianyang lay empty; righteous followers gathered from the four quarters; sweeping away the embers, victory was within a foot's reach.
translations.idiomatic: Hong fled west in rout, abandoning banners and troops; Xianyang stood empty; loyal forces gathered from every side; the last embers could be swept away and victory was at hand.

sentences.zh: 」天子慰勞高祖曰：「逋寇阻隘，晏安假日，舉斧函谷，規延王誅，群師勤王，將離寒暑。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven comforted and praised the High Ancestor: "The fugitive rebel blocks the passes and idles in false peace; he raises the axe at Hangu and plots to prolong his doomed reign; the hosts loyal to the throne have marched through cold and heat."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the High Ancestor: "The rebel holds the passes in false security, threatens at Hangu, and seeks to delay his doom while loyal armies have marched through winter and summer."

sentences.zh: 公躬秉鈇鉞，棱威首塗，戎略載脂，則郊壘疊卷，崤陝甫踐，則潼塞開扃。

translations.literal: My lord personally bears the battle-axe; your awestriking might leads the way; when the war plan is oiled and set, the suburban ramparts fold away layer by layer; when Xia and Shan are first trodden, the Tong passes open their gates.
translations.idiomatic: You bear the imperial axe in person; your majesty leads the van. Where your strategy advances, outer defenses fall; once Xia and Shan are crossed, the Tong passes open.

sentences.zh: 姚泓窘逼，棄城送死，藍田偏師，覆之霸川，甲首成林，俘獲蔽野，偽首奔迸，華、戎雲集，積紀逋寇，旦夕夷殄。

translations.literal: Yao Hong, hard pressed, abandoned his city and rushed to his death; the detached force at Lantian overthrew him at Bachuan; severed heads formed forests and captives covered the fields; the false ruler fled in panic; Chinese and barbarians gathered like clouds; the rebel of many years will be extinguished within days.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong, cornered, abandoned his city to his doom. The Lantian column destroyed him at Bachuan; heads piled like groves and captives filled the plain. The false ruler fled in panic; Chinese and barbarians rallied; the rebel of long standing will be wiped out within days.

sentences.zh: 」長安既平，高祖燕於文昌殿，舉酒賜田子曰：「咸陽之平，卿之功也。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, the High Ancestor feasted in the Wenchang Hall, raised his cup, and granted wine to Tianzi, saying: "The pacification of Xianyang is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, the High Ancestor feasted in the Wenchang Hall and raised his cup to Tianzi: "The pacification of Xianyang is your doing."

sentences.zh: 」即以咸陽相賞。

translations.literal: He thereupon rewarded him with Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 田子謝曰：「咸陽之平，此實聖略所振，武臣效節，田子何力之有。

translations.literal: Tianzi declined: "The pacification of Xianyang was truly roused by sacred strategy; military officers offered their loyalty—what strength had Tianzi!"
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi demurred: "Xianyang fell by your sacred strategy; we officers only did our duty—what credit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 」即授咸陽、始平二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was thereupon appointed Administrator of the two commanderies of Xianyang and Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed administrator of Xianyang and Shiping.

sentences.zh: 大軍既還，桂陽公義真留鎮長安，以田子為安西中兵參軍、龍驤將軍、始平太守。

translations.literal: When the great army had returned, the Duke of Guiyang Yizhen remained to garrison Chang'an; Tianzi was made central army military adviser of Pacify-the-West, General of Agile Cavalry, and Administrator of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew, Duke Yizhen of Guiyang stayed to garrison Chang'an, and Tianzi was made central army adviser on the Pacify-the-West staff, General of Agile Cavalry, and administrator of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 時佛佛來寇，田子與安西司馬王鎮惡俱出北地禦之。

translations.literal: At the time Fotu came to raid; Tianzi and Pacify-the-West Chief Administrator Wang Zhen'e both went out to Beidi to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fotu raided, Tianzi and Wang Zhen'e, chief administrator of Pacify-the-West, marched into Beidi to meet him.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖將還，田子及傅弘之等並以鎮惡家在關中，不可保信，屢言之高祖。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the High Ancestor was about to return, Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi and others all said that because Zhen'e's family was in Guanzhong he could not be trusted, and they repeatedly told the High Ancestor so.
translations.idiomatic: Before the High Ancestor withdrew, Tianzi, Fu Hongzhi, and others warned repeatedly that Wang Zhen'e, with his family in Guanzhong, could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「今留卿文武將士精兵萬人。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said: "I now leave you civil and military officers with ten thousand crack troops."
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor said, "I leave you ten thousand elite troops, civil and military alike."

sentences.zh: 彼若欲為不善，正足自滅耳。

translations.literal: If he wishes to do wrong, he will only destroy himself.
translations.idiomatic: If he turns traitor, he will only destroy himself.

sentences.zh: 勿復多言。

translations.literal: Speak no more of it.
translations.idiomatic: Say no more of it.

sentences.zh: 」及俱出北地，論者謂鎮惡欲盡殺諸南人，以數千人送義真南還，因據關中反叛。

translations.literal: When they all went out to Beidi, opinion held that Zhen'e wished to kill all the southerners, send several thousand men escorting Yizhen southward, and then hold Guanzhong and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When they marched into Beidi together, rumor held that Zhen'e meant to slaughter the southerners, send a few thousand men to escort Yizhen south, and seize Guanzhong in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 田子與弘之謀，矯高祖令誅之，並力破佛佛，安關中，然後南還謝罪。

translations.literal: Tianzi and Hongzhi plotted to forge an order from the High Ancestor to execute him, join forces to defeat Fotu, secure Guanzhong, and then return south to confess their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi and Hongzhi plotted to forge an order from the High Ancestor, kill him, defeat Fotu together, secure Guanzhong, then return south to accept punishment.

sentences.zh: 田子宗人沈敬仁驍果有勇力，田子於弘之營內請鎮惡計事，使敬仁於坐殺之，率左右數十人自歸義真。

translations.literal: Tianzi's clansman Shen Jingren was fierce and brave; within Hongzhi's camp Tianzi invited Zhen'e to discuss affairs and had Jingren kill him at the seat; he then led several dozen followers to surrender to Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi's kinsman Shen Jingren was bold and strong. In Hongzhi's camp Tianzi summoned Zhen'e on pretense of counsel and had Jingren kill him at table; then he took several dozen followers to Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 長史王脩收殺田子於長安稿倉門外，是歲，義熙十四年正月十五日也。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Wang Xiu arrested and executed Tianzi outside the Gaocang gate of Chang'an; it was the fifteenth day of the first month of the fourteenth year of Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Wang Xiu had Tianzi executed outside Chang'an's Gaocang Gate on the fifteenth of the first month, Yixi 14.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 田子初以功應封，因此事寢。

translations.literal: Tianzi had originally merited enfeoffment for his achievements, but because of this affair it was set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi had earned a fief for his deeds, but because of this affair the grant was never made.

sentences.zh: 高祖表天子，以田子卒發狂易，不深罪也。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor memorialized the Son of Heaven that Tianzi had died in a fit of madness and should not be deeply punished.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor reported to the emperor that Tianzi had died in a fit of madness and asked that he not be heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 無子，弟林子以第二子亮為後。

translations.literal: He had no son; his younger brother Linzi made his second son Liang his heir.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his younger brother Linzi adopted his second son Liang as heir.

sentences.zh: 亮，字道明，清操好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Liang, styled Daoming, had pure conduct, loved learning, and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, courtesy name Daoming, was a man of pure conduct who loved learning and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，州辟從事。

translations.literal: Before capping age the province summoned him as an aide.
translations.idiomatic: Before his capping the province recruited him as an aide.

sentences.zh: 會稽太守孟顗在郡不法，亮糾劾免官，又言災異，轉西曹主簿。

translations.literal: Meng Yi, Administrator of Kuaiji, acted unlawfully in the commandery; Liang impeached him and had him removed from office, also reported omens and portents, and was transferred to chief clerk of the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Yi, administrator of Kuaiji, broke the law in office, Liang impeached him and secured his dismissal, reported celestial omens, and was made chief clerk of the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時三吳水淹，穀貴民饑，刺史彭城王義康使立議以救民急，亮議以：「東土災荒，民凋榖踴，富民蓄米，日成其價。

translations.literal: At the time the Three Wu regions were flooded, grain was costly and the people starved; the Governor, the Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, had proposals drafted to relieve the people's distress; Liang proposed: "The eastern lands suffer disaster and famine; the people are wasted and grain prices soar; the rich hoard rice and daily raise its price."
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck the Three Wu and grain prices soared, Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, as governor, called for relief plans. Liang proposed: "The east is stricken; the people are ruined and grain grows dearer daily as the rich hoard rice."

sentences.zh: 宜班下所在，隱其虛實，令積蓄之家，聽留一年儲，餘皆勒使糶貨，為制平價，此所謂常道行於百世，權宜用於一時也。

translations.literal: Orders should be sent everywhere to ascertain true stocks; households with stores should be allowed to keep one year's supply, and the rest compelled to sell at regulated fair prices—this is what is called the constant Way enduring for a hundred generations and expedient measures applied for a single time.
translations.idiomatic: Orders should go out to audit stores everywhere: hoarders may keep one year's supply, but the rest must be sold at a fair fixed price—the constant rule for all ages, with a timely expedient for the crisis.

sentences.zh: 又緣淮歲豐，邑富地穰，麥既已登，黍粟行就，可析其估賦，仍就交市，三吳饑民，即以貸給，使強壯轉運，以贍老弱。

translations.literal: Moreover along the Huai the harvest is abundant, the districts rich and the land fertile; wheat is already in, millet and grain are nearly ripe; their assessed levies may be divided off and exchanged in trade; the starving people of the Three Wu may be lent grain at once, with the strong transporting it to support the old and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Huai the harvest is rich; wheat is in and millet nearly ripe. Take part of their tax grain for exchange and lend it to the starving Three Wu, with the able-bodied transporting it to feed the old and weak.

sentences.zh: 且酒有喉脣之利，而非餐餌所資，尤宜禁斷，以息游費。

translations.literal: Moreover wine gratifies the throat and lips but is not food for sustenance; it should especially be forbidden to end wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Wine pleases the palate but does not nourish; it should be banned to stop wasteful spending.

sentences.zh: 」即並施行。

translations.literal: All these measures were at once put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: All these measures were adopted at once.

sentences.zh: 世祖出鎮歷陽，行參征虜軍事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu went out to garrison Liyang, Liang served as mobile military adviser on the Pacify-the-Captive staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Shizu took up his post at Liyang, Liang served as mobile adviser on the Pacify-the-Captive staff.

sentences.zh: 民有盜發塚者，罪所近村民，與符伍遭劫不赴救同坐。

translations.literal: When the people robbed opened tombs, nearby villagers were punished; those in the same registry group who failed to go to the rescue when robbery occurred were punished equally.
translations.idiomatic: When graves were robbed, nearby villagers were punished, and registry neighbors who failed to respond to a robbery were punished the same way.

sentences.zh: 亮議曰：

translations.literal: Liang proposed:
translations.idiomatic: Liang argued:

sentences.zh: 尋發塚之情，事止竊盜，徒以侵亡犯死，故同之嚴科。

translations.literal: Considering the circumstances of tomb-opening, the act is merely theft; only because it violates the dead and incurs capital punishment is it equated with severe statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Grave-robbing is essentially theft; only because it violates the dead and carries the death penalty is it treated like the gravest crimes.

sentences.zh: 夫穿掘之侶，必銜枚以晦其跡；

translations.literal: Those who dig and tunnel must keep silent to conceal their tracks;
translations.idiomatic: Grave-robbers work in silence to hide their tracks;

sentences.zh: 劫掠之黨，必歡呼以威其事。

translations.literal: bands of robbers must shout aloud to overawe in their deeds.
translations.idiomatic: robbers shout aloud to terrify their victims.

sentences.zh: 故赴凶赫者易，應潛密者難。

translations.literal: Therefore it is easy to rush to glaring violence but hard to respond to hidden secrecy.
translations.idiomatic: It is easy to answer open violence but hard to detect secret crime.

sentences.zh: 且山原為無人之鄉，丘壟非恆途所踐，至於防救，不得比之村郭。

translations.literal: Moreover hills and plains are uninhabited country; mounds and tombs are not paths regularly traveled—as to prevention and rescue, they cannot be compared with villages and wards.
translations.idiomatic: Hills and wilds are uninhabited; tombs lie off the common road—defense and rescue there cannot be judged by village standards.

sentences.zh: 督實效名，理與劫異，則符伍之坐，居宜降矣。

translations.literal: When supervising real results and verifying names, the principle differs from robbery; then the punishment of registry groups should rightly be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: When the facts are examined, the case differs from robbery, and registry-group penalties should be lightened.

sentences.zh: 又結罰之科，雖有同符伍之限，而無遠近之斷。

translations.literal: Moreover the statutes on collective punishment, though they have the same limits as registry groups, lack any distinction of distance.
translations.idiomatic: The collective-punishment statutes, though they bind registry groups, set no limit of distance.

sentences.zh: 夫塚無村界，當以比近坐之。

translations.literal: Tombs have no village boundaries; punishment should fall on those nearest.
translations.idiomatic: Tombs have no village bounds; only those nearby should be held liable.

sentences.zh: 若不域之以界，則數步之內，與十里之外，便應同罹其責。

translations.literal: If no boundary is set, then those within a few paces and those ten li away would bear the same guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Without a boundary, those a few steps away and those ten li distant would share the same punishment.

sentences.zh: 防民之禁，不可頓去，止非之憲，宜當其律。

translations.literal: The prohibitions guarding the people cannot be suddenly removed; the statutes restraining wrongdoing should fit the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Popular safeguards cannot be abolished at once, but penalties should fit the offense.

sentences.zh: 愚謂相去百步同赴告不時者，一歲刑，自此以外，差不及罰。

translations.literal: I hold that those within a hundred paces who likewise fail to report in time should receive one year's punishment; beyond that distance, penalties should not apply.
translations.idiomatic: I propose one year's punishment for neighbors within a hundred paces who fail to report in time; beyond that, no penalty.

sentences.zh: 又啟太祖陳府事曰：「伏見西府兵士，或年幾八十，而猶伏隸；

translations.literal: He again memorialized the Grand Ancestor on commandery affairs: "I observe that among the western headquarters soldiers, some are nearly eighty and still serve as conscripts;"
translations.idiomatic: He again reported to the Grand Ancestor: "Among the western headquarters troops, some are nearly eighty and still serve as conscripts;"

sentences.zh: 或年始七歲，而已從役。

translations.literal: some are only seven and already on service.
translations.idiomatic: others are only seven and already on duty.

sentences.zh: 衰耗之體，氣用湮微，兒弱之軀，肌膚未實，而使伏勤昏稚，騖苦傾晚，於理既薄，為益實輕。

translations.literal: Bodies worn and spent have vital breath faint and slight; children's frames have flesh not yet firm—yet they are made to labor from dawn to dusk and rush hardship into old age; in principle this is thin, and the benefit is truly slight.
translations.idiomatic: The aged have little strength left; children are not fully grown—yet both are driven from dawn to dusk. It is unjust and of little use.

sentences.zh: 書制休老以六十為限，役少以十五為制，若力不周務，故當粗存優減。

translations.literal: The written regulations set retirement at sixty and minimum service at fifteen; when strength cannot meet the task, some allowance and reduction should be kept.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes set retirement at sixty and service from fifteen; when men cannot meet the work, they should receive some relief.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「前已令卿兄改革，尋值遷回，竟是不施行耶？

translations.literal: An edict said: "Earlier I ordered your elder brother to reform this; soon afterward he was transferred—was it in the end not carried out?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "I ordered your elder brother to reform this, but he was transferred—was it never done?"

sentences.zh: 今更敕西府也。

translations.literal: Now I again order the western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: I order the western headquarters again now.

sentences.zh: 」時營創城府，功課嚴促，亮又陳之曰：「經始城宇，莫非造創，基築既廣，夫課又嚴，不計其勞，苟務其速，以歲月之事，求不日之成。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery seat and walls were being built, labor quotas were strict and urgent; Liang again submitted: "In founding city walls, everything is new construction; the foundations are broad and the labor quotas severe; labor is not counted, only speed is sought—a task of months pursued for completion in days."
translations.idiomatic: While the city walls were being built, quotas were harsh. Liang reported again: "Building anew on this scale with severe quotas ignores men's labor and demands in days what should take months."

sentences.zh: 比見役人未明上作，閉鼓乃休，呈課既多，理有不逮。

translations.literal: Recently I have seen corvée laborers begin before dawn and rest only when the drums close; the quotas presented are so many that fulfillment is impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers now work from before dawn until nightfall; the quotas set are impossible to meet.

sentences.zh: 至於息日，拘備關限，方涉暑雨，多有死病，頃日所承，亦頗有逃逸。

translations.literal: As for rest days, they are confined under guard; just as summer heat and rain arrive, many die of illness; in recent days I have heard that quite a few have fled.
translations.idiomatic: Even rest days are restricted; in the summer rains many fall ill and die, and recently many have fled.

sentences.zh: 竊惟此既內藩，事殊外鎮，撫蒞之宜，無繫早晚。

translations.literal: I reflect that this is an inner principality, unlike an outer garrison; the manner of governing need not depend on haste from dawn to dusk.
translations.idiomatic: This is an inner principality, not a frontier post—governance need not turn on dawn-to-dusk haste.

sentences.zh: 若得少寬其工課，稍均其優劇，徒隸既苦，易以悅加，考其卒功，廢闕無幾。

translations.literal: If the labor quotas were slightly eased and hard and light tasks somewhat balanced, the conscripts, though suffering, would more easily take pleasure in their work; judging the final achievement, little would be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Ease the quotas slightly and balance hard and light tasks; the laborers would work more willingly, and little would be lost in the end.

sentences.zh: 臣聞不居其職，不謀其事，庖割有主，尸不越樽，豈臣疏小，所當預議。

translations.literal: I have heard that one not in his office does not plan its affairs; the cook has his master, the steward does not step past the wine-jar—how should one of my slight rank take part in such deliberation!
translations.idiomatic: I know one should not meddle outside one's office—yet how should a man of my humble rank speak on such matters!

sentences.zh: 但臣泳恩歲厚，服義累世，苟是所懷，忘其常體。

translations.literal: Yet I have bathed in grace for many years and served with loyalty for generations; when something weighs on my heart, I forget ordinary propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I have long enjoyed your grace and served your house for generations; when something weighs on my heart, I forget my place.

sentences.zh: 」詔答曰：「啟之甚佳。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "Your report is excellent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your report is excellent."

sentences.zh: 此亦由來常患，比屢敕之，猶復如此，甚為無理。

translations.literal: This too has long been a chronic ill; I have repeatedly ordered reform, yet it remains thus—most unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: This has long been a chronic abuse; I have ordered reform again and again, yet it persists—most unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 近復令孟休宣旨，想當不同，卿比可密觀其優劇也。

translations.literal: Recently I again had Meng Xiu proclaim the edict; I trust matters will be different; you may now secretly observe whether hard and light tasks are balanced.
translations.idiomatic: I have just sent Meng Xiu with fresh orders; matters should improve. Watch in secret whether the work is fairly apportioned.

sentences.zh: 」始興王濬臨揚州，復為主簿、秣陵令，善擿奸伏，有非必禽。

translations.literal: " When the Prince of Shixing, Jun, took charge of Yangzhou, Liang again served as registrar and magistrate of Moling; he was skilled at exposing hidden wrongdoing, and whenever there was fault he always seized the culprit.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Liu Jun of Shixing took up his post at Yangzhou, Liang again served as registrar and magistrate of Moling. He had a gift for uncovering hidden crimes, and whenever he found wrongdoing he always caught those responsible.

sentences.zh: 太祖稱其能，入為尚書都官郎。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor praised his ability, and he entered the capital as Director of the Masters of Writing in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor praised his talent, and Liang was summoned to the capital as Director in the Bureau of Punishments under the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 襄陽地接邊關，江左來未有皇子重鎮。

translations.literal: Xiangyang bordered the frontier passes; since the south of the Yangzi no imperial prince had held so important a post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang lay on the frontier, and since the Eastern Jin no imperial prince had been stationed at so weighty a command.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十二年，世祖出為撫軍將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Yuanjia, Emperor Shizu went out as General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 22 the future Emperor Shizu took up the posts of General Who Pacifies the Army and Inspector of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 天子甚留心，以舊宛比接二關，咫尺崤、陝，蓋襄陽之北捍，且表裏強蠻，盤帶疆場，以亮為南陽太守，加揚武將軍。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven paid close attention; because Old Wan adjoined the two passes and was close to Xiao and Shan, it was essentially the northern bulwark of Xiangyang; moreover, inside and outside were powerful barbarians encircling the borderlands— he appointed Liang Administrator of Nanyang and added the title General Who Displays Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took great interest in the matter. Old Wan adjoined the two passes and lay within a stone's throw of Xiao and Shan; it was the northern shield of Xiangyang, with powerful barbarians pressing the frontier both within and without. He therefore made Liang Administrator of Nanyang and promoted him to General Who Displays Martiality.

sentences.zh: 邊蠻畏服，皆納賦調，有數村狡猾，亮悉誅之。

translations.literal: The frontier barbarians feared and submitted; all paid taxes and corvée levies; several villages were crafty and cunning— Liang executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier tribes submitted in fear and paid their taxes and levies. A few villages remained obstinate and deceitful, and Liang put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 遣吏巡行諸縣，孤寡老疾不能自存者，皆就蠲養，耆年老齒，歲時有餼。

translations.literal: He sent officials to tour the counties; orphans, widows, elderly, and sick who could not support themselves were all exempted and cared for; the very aged received seasonal rations.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officials to inspect the counties. Orphans, widows, the elderly, and the sick who could not support themselves were exempted from levies and given relief, and the very old received regular seasonal provisions.

sentences.zh: 時儒學崇建，亮開置庠序，訓授生徒。

translations.literal: At that time Confucian learning was highly promoted; Liang opened schools and instructed students.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian learning was then greatly encouraged, and Liang established schools and taught students.

sentences.zh: 民多發塚，並婚嫁違法，皆嚴為條禁。

translations.literal: Many among the people opened graves, and marriages also violated the law; he strictly established regulations forbidding these.
translations.idiomatic: Grave-robbing was widespread, and marriages often broke the law; he imposed strict regulations against both.

sentences.zh: 郡界有古時石堨，蕪廢歲久，亮籤世祖修治之，曰：「施生興業，首教農畝，立民崇政，訓本播穡，故能殷邦康俗，禮節用成。

translations.literal: Within the commandery was an ancient stone dyke long abandoned to waste; Liang memorialized Emperor Shizu to repair it, saying: "To nourish life and establish enterprise, one must first teach farming; to establish the people and exalt governance, one must instruct in fundamentals and spread cultivation— thus states become prosperous and customs wholesome, and ritual and order are achieved.
translations.idiomatic: An ancient stone dyke within the commandery had lain ruined for many years. Liang petitioned Emperor Shizu to restore it, writing: "To sustain life and build prosperity one must first teach farming; to settle the people and elevate government one must train them in fundamentals and spread cultivation. Only then do states flourish, customs grow sound, and ritual and order take shape.

sentences.zh: 頃北洛侵蕪，南宛雕毀，獫狁肆凶。

translations.literal: Recently the northern Luoyang region lies waste, southern Wan is ruined, and the Xianyun run rampant with violence.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the lands north of Luoyang have fallen to ruin, southern Wan lies devastated, and the northern tribes have run wild with violence.

sentences.zh: 犬夷充疆，遠肅烽驛，近虞郊閈，遂使沃衍弗井，巨防莫修，窘力輟耕，闕於分地，凶荒無待，流冗及今。

translations.literal: The Di barbarians filled the borders; distant beacon and relay stations were subdued, nearby suburbs and gates were anxious; thus fertile fields went unplowed, great dykes unrepaired, strained strength ceased cultivation, land was not allotted; disaster and famine needed no waiting, and displaced people suffer to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian forces filled the frontier. Distant beacons fell silent while nearby suburbs lived in fear. Fertile fields went untilled, great dykes unrepaired, farmers too exhausted to plow, and land left undistributed. Famine and ruin needed no invitation, and displaced people still suffer the consequences.

sentences.zh: 禮化孚內，威禁清外，斯實去盜修畎，昭農緒稼之時，弘圖廣務，拓土祈年之日。

translations.literal: When ritual transformation fills within and majesty and prohibition clear without, this is truly the time to remove thieves and repair fields, to manifest the enterprise of agriculture, to expand grand designs and broad affairs, to extend territory and pray for good harvest.
translations.idiomatic: When civilizing ritual fills the realm within and authority keeps the frontier clear without, it is precisely the moment to drive off bandits, restore the fields, renew agriculture, broaden great undertakings, and extend the domain in hope of abundant harvests.

sentences.zh: 殿下降心育物，振民復古，且方提封榛棘，綏入殊荒。

translations.literal: Your Highness lowers your heart to nurture things, stirs the people and restores antiquity; moreover you are now raising boundaries from brambles and thorns and pacifying entry into strange lands.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has bent your heart to nurturing the people, rousing them to restore the ways of old, and are now clearing thorn-choked borders and bringing order to distant wilds.

sentences.zh: 竊見郡境有舊石堨，區野腴潤，實為神皋，而蕪決稍積，久廢其利，凡管所見，謂宜創立。

translations.literal: I have seen within the commandery an old stone dyke; the district land is rich and moist— a truly fertile tract— but breaches have gradually accumulated and it has long been abandoned to waste; all I have seen, I say should be newly established.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed an old stone dyke in the commandery whose surrounding fields are rich and moist—a truly fertile tract. Yet breaches have piled up over time and its benefits have long been lost. In my judgment it should be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 昔文翁守官，起沃成產，偉連撫民，開奧增業，惠昭二邦，庸列兩漢。

translations.literal: In antiquity Wen Weng in office made barren land fertile and productive; Wei Lian in comforting the people opened deep lands and increased enterprise— their kindness illumined two states, their merit ranks them among the two Han.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Wen Weng in office turned wasteland into abundance, and Wei Lian in governing the people opened hidden lands and expanded production. Their benevolence lit up two kingdoms, and their achievements rank among the great ministers of the two Han dynasties.

sentences.zh: 雖效政圖功，不見所絕，聯事惟忝，憂同職同。

translations.literal: Although they achieved effective governance and plotted merit without being surpassed in fame, I in my joint service am only ashamed— my worry is the same office, the same duty.
translations.idiomatic: Though they achieved effective rule and planned great works without equal, I can only feel ashamed in holding a similar post and bear the same burden of office.

sentences.zh: 」囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗囗又修治馬人陂，民獲其利。

translations.literal: [Text lost.] He also repaired the Mare-human Dyke, and the people obtained its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: [Text lost.] He also restored the Mare-human Dyke, and the people reaped its benefits.

sentences.zh: 在任四年，遷南譙王義宣司空中兵參軍。

translations.literal: After four years in office, he was transferred to central army military adviser under Staff Director for the Prince of Nanqiao, Yi Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office he was transferred to serve as central army adviser on the staff of Prince Liu Yixuan of Nanqiao.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「陝西心膂須才，故授卿此職。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The heart and backbone of the western passes require talent; therefore I appoint you to this office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "The western frontier needs able men at its core; that is why I give you this post.

sentences.zh: 」隨王誕鎮襄陽，復為後軍中兵，領義成太守。

translations.literal: " When the Prince of Sui, Dan, garrisoned Xiangyang, Liang again served as rear army central army commander and concurrently Administrator of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Liu Dan of Sui took command at Xiangyang, Liang again served as central army commander of the rear army and concurrently as Administrator of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 亮蒞官清約，為太祖所嘉，賜以車馬服玩，前後累積。

translations.literal: Liang in office was pure and frugal, praised by the Grand Ancestor, and granted carriages, horses, clothing, and curios— accumulated over time.
translations.idiomatic: Liang governed with purity and restraint, won the Grand Ancestor's praise, and received carriages, horses, clothing, and fine objects in gifts that accumulated over the years.
