sentences.zh: 每遠方貢獻絕國勳器，輒班賚焉。

translations.literal: Whenever distant lands sent tribute of exotic treasures, he would always distribute gifts to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever distant lands sent tribute of rare and exotic objects, Liang was always among those rewarded.

sentences.zh: 又賜書二千卷。

translations.literal: He was also granted two thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given two thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒官，時年四十七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died in office, at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia he died in office at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 所著詩、賦、頌、贊、三言、誄、哀辭、祭告請雨文、樂府、挽歌、連珠、教記、白事、箋、表、籤、議一百八十九首。

translations.literal: His writings numbered one hundred eighty-nine pieces: poetry, fu, eulogies, praises, three-character texts, dirges, mourning compositions, rain-prayer liturgies, yuefu, elegies, linked pearls, admonitions, memorial reports, letters, petitions, memos, and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He left one hundred eighty-nine works, including poems, fu, eulogies, praises, three-character pieces, dirges, mourning compositions, rain-prayer texts, yuefu songs, elegies, linked pearls, admonitions, reports, letters, petitions, memos, and proposals.

sentences.zh: 林子，字敬士，田子弟也。

translations.literal: Linzi, styled Jingshi, was the younger brother of Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi, courtesy name Jingshi, was the younger brother of Shen Tianzi.

sentences.zh: 少有大度，年數歲，隨王父在京口。

translations.literal: From youth he had great breadth; at several years of age he followed his grandfather to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed unusual breadth of character. At only a few years old he went with his grandfather to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 王恭見而奇之，曰：「此兒王子師之流也。

translations.literal: Wang Gong saw him and marveled, saying: "This boy is of the same sort as Wang Zishi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong saw him and was struck by the boy, saying, "This child is cut from the same cloth as Wang Zishi.

sentences.zh: 」與眾人共見遺寶，咸爭趨之，林子直去不顧。

translations.literal: " When everyone together saw abandoned treasure, they all rushed to grab it; Linzi walked straight away without looking.
translations.idiomatic: " Once, when he and others came upon abandoned valuables, everyone rushed to seize them, but Linzi walked straight on without a glance.

sentences.zh: 年十三，遇家禍，時雖逃竄，而哀號晝夜不絕聲。

translations.literal: At thirteen he encountered family calamity; though fleeing at the time, he wailed day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he suffered a family catastrophe. Though he was fleeing for his life, he wailed day and night without stopping.

sentences.zh: 王母謂之曰：「汝當忍死強視，何為空自殄絕。

translations.literal: His grandmother said to him: "You ought to force yourself to live and look about— why destroy yourself for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother said to him, "You must force yourself to live on and keep your eyes open. Why throw your life away for nothing?

sentences.zh: 」林子曰：「家門酷橫，無復假日之心，直以至仇未復，故且苟存爾。

translations.literal: " Linzi said: "Our family has suffered cruel wrong; I no longer have heart to spare for anything else— I only live on because my greatest enemy is not yet revenged.
translations.idiomatic: " Linzi replied, "Our family has suffered cruel injustice, and I have no heart left for anything else. I endure only because my greatest enemy is not yet avenged.

sentences.zh: 」一門既陷妖黨，兄弟並應從誅，逃伏草澤，常慮及禍，而沈預家甚強富，志相陷滅。

translations.literal: " The whole clan had fallen into the sorcerer's faction; the brothers all deserved execution; they hid in marshes and wilds, constantly fearing disaster; but the Shen Yu family was very powerful and rich, intent on destroying them.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole clan had been implicated in the sorcerer rebellion; the brothers all faced execution. They hid in marshes and wild country, living in constant fear, while the Shen Yu family, powerful and wealthy, was determined to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 林子與諸兄晝藏夜出，即貨所居宅，營墓葬父祖諸叔，凡六喪，儉而有禮。

translations.literal: Linzi and his elder brothers hid by day and went out by night; they immediately sold their residence, arranging burials for father, grandfathers, and uncles— six funerals in all, frugal yet with proper rite.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi and his brothers hid by day and ventured out by night. They sold their house at once and arranged burials for their father, grandfathers, and uncles—six funerals in all, carried out with frugality but proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 時生業已盡，老弱甚多，東土饑荒，易子而食，外迫國網，內畏強仇，沈伏山草，無所投厝。

translations.literal: By then livelihood was exhausted, with many elderly and weak; the eastern lands suffered famine, people exchanged children to eat; pressured without by the imperial net, feared within by the powerful enemy; they lay hidden in mountain grass with nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: By then their livelihood was gone and many among them were old or weak. Famine ravaged the eastern lands until people exchanged children to eat. Hunted by the imperial law without and menaced by their powerful enemy within, they lay hidden in the hills with nowhere to go.

sentences.zh: 時孫恩屢出會稽，諸將東討者相續，劉牢之、高素之放縱其下，虜暴縱橫，獨高祖軍政嚴明，無所侵犯。

translations.literal: At that time Sun En repeatedly raided from Kuaiji; generals sent east in succession; Liu Laozhi and Gao Suzhi's troops looted and ravaged everywhere— only the High Ancestor's army and discipline were strict, without encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En repeatedly raided from Kuaiji, and one eastern campaign followed another. The troops of Liu Laozhi and Gao Suzhi plundered unchecked, but the High Ancestor's army alone maintained strict discipline and did not molest the people.

sentences.zh: 林子乃自歸曰：「妖賊擾亂，僕一門悉被驅逼，父祖諸叔，同罹禍難，猶複偷生天壤者，正以仇讎未復，親老漂寄爾。

translations.literal: Linzi then came of his own accord and said: "The sorcerer rebels disturb the realm; my whole household was driven into it; father, grandfathers, and uncles alike suffered calamity; the reason we still live on beneath heaven is only that our enemies are not yet avenged and our elders drift in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi then came forward of his own accord and said, "The rebel sorcerers have thrown the realm into chaos. My whole household was forced into their ranks; my father, grandfathers, and uncles all suffered the same disaster. The only reason we still live beneath heaven is that our enemies are not yet avenged and our elders remain adrift in exile.

sentences.zh: 今日見將軍伐惡旌善，是有道之師，謹率老弱，歸罪請命。

translations.literal: Today I see the general punishing evil and raising good— this is an army of the Way; I respectfully lead the elderly and weak to submit and beg for our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Today I see Your Lordship punishing evil and honoring good—an army of the Way. I therefore bring the old and weak of my household to submit and beg for our lives.

sentences.zh: 」因流涕哽咽，三軍為之感動。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wept and choked with sobs; the whole army was moved.
translations.idiomatic: " As he spoke he wept and choked with sobs, and the whole army was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚奇之，謂曰：「君既是國家罪人，強讎又在鄉里，唯當見隨還京，可得無恙。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was greatly impressed and said: "You are after all a criminal of the state; your powerful enemy is still in your native place— you should only come follow me back to the capital, then you can be unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor was greatly impressed and said, "You are still a criminal in the eyes of the state, and your powerful enemy remains in your home district. You should come with me back to the capital; only then can you be safe.

sentences.zh: 」乃載以別船，遂盡室移京口，高祖分宅給焉。

translations.literal: " He had him carried on a separate boat; they moved the entire household to Jingkou; the High Ancestor allocated a residence for them.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Linzi carried on a separate boat, moved the whole family to Jingkou, and allotted them a house.

sentences.zh: 博覽眾書，留心文義，從高祖克京城，進平都邑。

translations.literal: He read widely among all books and attended to literary meaning; he followed the High Ancestor in capturing the capital region and advanced to pacify the capital city.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and attended carefully to literary meaning. He followed the High Ancestor in the capture of the capital region and the pacification of the capital itself.

sentences.zh: 時年十八，身長七尺五寸。

translations.literal: At that time he was eighteen, seven feet five inches in height.
translations.idiomatic: He was then eighteen years old and seven feet five inches tall.

sentences.zh: 沈預慮林子為害，常被甲持戈。

translations.literal: Shen Yu feared Linzi would harm him and often wore armor carrying a spear.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yu, fearing Linzi would harm him, often wore armor and carried a spear.

sentences.zh: 至是林子與兄田子還東報讎。

translations.literal: At this point Linzi with his elder brother Tianzi returned east to avenge themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At that point Linzi and his elder brother Tianzi returned east to take revenge.

sentences.zh: 五月夏節日至，預正大集會，子弟盈堂，林子兄弟挺身直入，斬預首，男女無長幼悉屠之，以預首祭父、祖墓。

translations.literal: When the fifth-month Summer Festival day arrived, Yu was holding a great gathering with sons and nephews filling the hall; the Linzi brothers went straight in, beheaded Yu, slaughtered men and women of all ages, and offered Yu's head at the tombs of father and grandfathers.
translations.idiomatic: On the Dragon Boat Festival in the fifth month Yu was holding a great gathering with sons and nephews filling the hall. The Linzi brothers went straight in, cut off Yu's head, slaughtered men and women of every age, and offered his head at the tombs of their father and grandfathers.

sentences.zh: 仍為本郡所命，毅又板為冠軍參軍，並不就。

translations.literal: The local commandery then appointed him, and Huan Yi also issued a commission as Champion Army military adviser— he accepted neither.
translations.idiomatic: The local commandery then offered him office, and Huan Yi also issued a commission as Champion Army military adviser, but he accepted neither.

sentences.zh: 林子以家門荼蓼，無複仕心，高祖敦逼，至彌年不起。

translations.literal: Linzi, because his family had suffered bitter hardship, had no further desire for office; the High Ancestor pressed him urgently, yet for a full year he would not rise to accept office.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family had suffered bitter hardship, Linzi had no wish to serve in office. The High Ancestor pressed him urgently, yet for a full year he refused to accept a post.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為揚州，辟為從事，謂曰：「卿何由遂得不仕。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor became Inspector of Yangzhou, he recruited him as staff officer and said: "How is it you persist in not serving office?
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor became Inspector of Yangzhou, he recruited Linzi as a staff officer and said, "How can you go on refusing office?

sentences.zh: 頃年相申，欲令萬物見卿此心爾。

translations.literal: In recent years I repeatedly urged you— I wanted all to see your heart in this.
translations.idiomatic: These past years I have urged you again and again because I wanted everyone to see where your heart truly lies.

sentences.zh: 」固辭不得已，然後就職，領建熙令，封資中縣五等侯，時年二十一。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined until he could not refuse, then accepted the post, concurrently Magistrate of Jianxi, enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Zizhong county, age twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: " Linzi declined until he could refuse no longer, then took office as Magistrate of Jianxi and was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Zizhong. He was twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 義熙五年，從伐鮮卑，行參鎮軍軍事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yixi, he followed the campaign against the Xianbei, serving on the Pacifying Army staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 5 he joined the campaign against the Xianbei as mobile adviser on the Pacifying Army staff.

sentences.zh: 大軍於臨朐交戰，賊遣虎班突騎馳軍後，林子率精勇東西奮擊，皆大破之。

translations.literal: The great army fought at Linqu; the enemy sent Tiger-pattern shock cavalry to charge the rear of the army; Linzi led elite warriors striking east and west with full force— all were greatly broken.
translations.idiomatic: The main army fought at Linqu. The enemy sent elite Tiger-pattern shock cavalry against the rear, but Linzi led crack troops in fierce strikes east and west and broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 慕容超退守廣固，複與劉敬宣攻其西隅。

translations.literal: Murong Chao retreated to defend Guanggu; again with Liu Jingxuan he attacked the western corner.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chao withdrew to defend Guanggu, and Linzi again joined Liu Jingxuan in attacking the western corner of the city.

sentences.zh: 廣固既平，而盧循奄至。

translations.literal: Once Guanggu was pacified, Lu Xun suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Guanggu had barely been taken when Lu Xun suddenly appeared.

sentences.zh: 初，循之下也，廣固未拔，循潛遣使結林子及宗人叔長。

translations.literal: Initially when Xun descended, Guanggu was not yet taken; Xun secretly sent envoys to win over Linzi and his clansman Shuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun first marched south, Guanggu had not yet fallen. He secretly sent envoys to win over Linzi and his clansman Shuzhang.

sentences.zh: 林子即密白高祖，叔長不以聞，反以循旨動林子。

translations.literal: Linzi immediately secretly reported to the High Ancestor; Shuzhang did not report it, but instead used Xun's message to sway Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi at once secretly informed the High Ancestor. Shuzhang did not report the approach, but instead tried to sway Linzi with Xun's message.

sentences.zh: 叔長素驍果，高祖以超未平，隱之，還至廣固，乃誅叔長。

translations.literal: Shuzhang was by nature fierce and resolute; the High Ancestor, because Murong Chao was not yet pacified, kept it secret; returning to Guanggu, he then executed Shuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhang was by nature fierce and resolute. Because Murong Chao was not yet defeated, the High Ancestor kept the matter secret until he returned to Guanggu, when he executed Shuzhang.

sentences.zh: 謂林子曰：「昔魏武在官渡，汝、兗之士，多懷貳心，唯李通獨斷大義，古今一也。

translations.literal: He said to Linzi: "In antiquity at Guandu, the men of Yu and Yan many harbored divided hearts— only Li Tong alone upheld the great righteousness; past and present are one case.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Linzi, "At Guandu in olden days, many men of Yu and Yan wavered in their loyalty, but Li Tong alone held to the greater cause. Past and present are the same.

sentences.zh: 」循至蔡洲，貴遊之徒，皆議還徙，唯林子請移家京邑，高祖怪而問之，對曰：「耿純盡室從戎，李典舉宗居魏。

translations.literal: " When Xun reached Caizhou, the noble travelers all debated retreating and relocating; only Linzi asked to move his family to the capital; the High Ancestor wondered and asked him; he replied: "Geng Chun brought his whole household to follow the campaign; Li Dian moved his whole clan to Wei territory.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xun reached Caizhou, the court nobles all debated retreat, but Linzi alone asked to move his family to the capital. The High Ancestor was surprised and questioned him. Linzi replied, "Geng Chun brought his whole household to war, and Li Dian settled his entire clan under Wei.

sentences.zh: 林子雖才非古人，實受恩深重。

translations.literal: Though Linzi's talent is not that of the ancients, I have truly received profound favor.
translations.idiomatic: I am no match for those ancients in talent, but I have received profound favor.

sentences.zh: 」高祖稱善久之。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor praised him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor praised him at length.

sentences.zh: 林子時領別軍於石頭，屢戰摧寇。

translations.literal: Linzi then commanded a detached army at Shitou and repeatedly fought, crushing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi then commanded a detached force at Shitou and repeatedly defeated the rebels in battle.

sentences.zh: 循每戰無功，乃偽揚聲當悉眾于白石步上，而設伏于南岸，故大軍初起白石，留林子與徐赤將斷拒查浦。

translations.literal: Each time Xun fought without success, he falsely proclaimed he would deploy his entire force at Baishi Step— but set ambushes on the south bank; thus when the great army first moved toward Baishi, Linzi and Xu Chi were left to block and hold Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun won no victory in battle after battle, so he falsely announced that he would mass his entire force at Baishi Step while setting ambushes on the south bank. When the main army therefore moved toward Baishi, Linzi and Xu Chi were left to block Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 林子乃進計曰：「此言妖詐，未必有實，宜深為之防。

translations.literal: Linzi then advanced a plan: "These words are demonic deceit and may not be real; we should deeply guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi then offered a plan: "This report is likely a ruse and may not be true. We should guard against it carefully.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「石頭城險，且淮柵甚固，留卿在後，足以守之。

translations.literal: " The High Ancestor said: "Shitou fortress is perilous, and moreover the Huai barricades are very solid— leaving you in the rear is sufficient to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: " The High Ancestor said, "Shitou is a strong fortress and the Huai barricades are solid. Leaving you in the rear is enough to hold them.

sentences.zh: 」大軍既去，賊果上，赤特將擊之。

translations.literal: The great army having gone, the bandits indeed came up river; Chi Te led troops to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the main army had departed, the rebels did come upstream, and Chi Te led his troops out to attack them.

sentences.zh: 林子曰：「賊聲往白石，而屢來挑戰，其情狀可知矣。

translations.literal: Linzi said: "The bandits proclaim they are going to Baishi, yet repeatedly come to challenge battle— their true intent can be known.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi said, "The rebels claim they are heading for Baishi, yet they keep coming to challenge us. Their real intent is clear.

sentences.zh: 賊養銳待期，而吾眾不盈二旅，難以有功。

translations.literal: The bandits husband their edge awaiting the appointed day; our force does not fill two brigades— it will be hard to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is husbanding his strength for the appointed day, while our force numbers less than two brigades. It will be hard to win a victory.

sentences.zh: 今距守此險，足以自固。

translations.literal: Now holding this perilous position at a distance, it is sufficient for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold this strong position, we can defend ourselves adequately.

sentences.zh: 若賊偽計不立，大軍尋反，君何患焉？

translations.literal: If the bandits' false scheme does not succeed, the great army will soon return— what worry have you?
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy's ruse fails, the main army will soon return. What is there to worry about?

sentences.zh: 」赤特曰：「今賊悉眾向白石，留者必皆羸老，以銳卒擊之，無不破也。

translations.literal: " Chi Te said: "Now the bandits' entire force is going to Baishi; those left behind must all be weak and old— with crack troops striking them, none will fail to be broken.
translations.idiomatic: " Chi Te said, "The rebels have sent their whole force toward Baishi. Those left behind must be weak and old. A strike with crack troops cannot fail to break them.

sentences.zh: 」便鼓噪而出，賊伏兵齊發，赤特軍果敗，棄軍奔北岸；

translations.literal: " He then beat drums and shouted as they went out; the bandits' hidden troops all sprang up; Chi Te's army was indeed defeated and abandoned the army fleeing to the north bank;
translations.idiomatic: " He beat drums and charged out. The enemy's hidden troops sprang up together, Chi Te's force was routed, and he abandoned his army and fled to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 林子率軍收赤特散兵，進戰，摧破之。

translations.literal: Linzi led the army to gather Chi Te's scattered troops, advanced to battle, and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi gathered Chi Te's scattered troops, advanced to battle, and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆乃更上銳卒，沿塘數里。

translations.literal: Xu Daofu then brought up more crack troops along the embankment for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Daofu then brought up fresh crack troops along the embankment for several li.

sentences.zh: 林子策之曰：「賊沿塘結陣，戰者不過一隊。

translations.literal: Linzi calculated: "The bandits array along the embankment— those fighting cannot exceed one unit at a time.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi assessed the situation and said, "The enemy is forming battle lines along the embankment, but only one unit can fight at a time.

sentences.zh: 今我據其津而厄其要，彼雖銳師數里，不敢過而東必也。

translations.literal: Now if we hold their crossing and choke the crucial point, though they have crack troops for several li, they will not dare pass eastward.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold their crossing and block the vital point, they may have crack troops strung out for miles, but they will not dare pass eastward.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃斷塘而鬥。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they blocked the embankment and fought.
translations.idiomatic: " They therefore blocked the embankment and gave battle.

sentences.zh: 久之，會朱齡石救至，與林子並勢，賊乃散走。

translations.literal: After a long while Zhu Lingshi's rescue arrived; together with Linzi they combined forces and the bandits scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After a long fight Zhu Lingshi's relief force arrived. He and Linzi combined strength, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 大軍至自白石，殺赤特以殉，以林子參中軍軍事。

translations.literal: The great army returned from Baishi; they killed Chi Te to expose as warning; Linzi was appointed staff officer on the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned from Baishi, Chi Te was executed as a warning to the troops, and Linzi was appointed adviser on the Central Army staff.

sentences.zh: 從征劉毅，轉參太尉軍事。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Yi and was transferred to Staff Director of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Liu Yi and was transferred to adviser on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 十一年，複從討司馬休之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he again followed in suppressing Sima Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again joined the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 高祖每征討，林子輒摧鋒居前，雖有營部，至於宵夕，輒敕還內侍。

translations.literal: Whenever the High Ancestor went on campaign, Linzi always broke the vanguard at the front; though he had a camp department, by nightfall he would always be ordered back to attend inside.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the High Ancestor took the field, Linzi always led the vanguard in breaking the enemy line. Though he had his own camp staff, each evening he was ordered back to attend the commander in person.

sentences.zh: 賊党郭亮之招集蠻眾，屯據武陵，武陵太守王鎮惡出奔，林子率軍討之，斬亮之於七里澗，納鎮惡。

translations.literal: The rebel party Guo Liangzhi gathered barbarian masses and entrenched at Wuling; Wuling Administrator Wang Zhen'e fled; Linzi led troops to attack, beheaded Liangzhi at Qili Stream, and restored Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Guo Liangzhi gathered tribal forces and seized Wuling. The administrator Wang Zhen'e fled, but Linzi led troops against him, cut off Liangzhi's head at Qili Stream, and restored Zhen'e to office.

sentences.zh: 武陵既平，複討魯軌於石城，軌棄眾奔襄陽，複追躡之。

translations.literal: Once Wuling was pacified, he again attacked Lu Gui at Shicheng; Gui abandoned his force and fled to Xiangyang; they pursued him again.
translations.idiomatic: After Wuling was pacified, he again attacked Lu Gui at Shicheng. Gui abandoned his troops and fled to Xiangyang, and Linzi pursued him.

sentences.zh: 襄陽既定，權留守江陵。

translations.literal: Once Xiangyang was settled, he was temporarily left to garrison Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang was secured, he was temporarily left to garrison Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高祖領平北將軍，林子以太尉參軍，複參平北軍事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the High Ancestor held the post of General Who Pacifies the North; Linzi as Grand Commandant staff officer again served on the Pacify-the-North staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the High Ancestor took the post of General Who Pacifies the North. Linzi, as adviser to the Grand Commandant, again served on the Pacify-the-North staff.

sentences.zh: 其冬，高祖伐羌，複參征西軍事，悉署三府中兵，加建武將軍，統軍為前鋒，從汴入河。

translations.literal: That winter the High Ancestor campaigned against the Qiang; again on the Pacify-the-West staff; he was put in charge of all central army troops of the three headquarters; added title General Who Establishes Martiality; commanded the army as vanguard, entering the Yellow River from Bian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the High Ancestor marched against the Qiang. Linzi again served on the Pacify-the-West staff, was put in charge of all central army troops of the three headquarters, promoted to General Who Establishes Martiality, and commanded the vanguard entering the Yellow River from Bian.

sentences.zh: 時襄邑降人董神虎有義兵千餘人，高祖欲綏懷初附，即板為太尉參軍，加揚武將軍，領兵從戎。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Shenhu of Xiangyi, a surrendered man, had righteous troops of over a thousand; the High Ancestor wished to soothe those newly attached and immediately issued a commission as Grand Commandant staff officer, added General Who Displays Martiality, leading troops on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dong Shenhu, a surrendered man of Xiangyi, had a volunteer force of more than a thousand. The High Ancestor wished to reassure those newly submitted and immediately commissioned him as adviser to the Grand Commandant with the added title General Who Displays Martiality, leading troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 林子率神虎攻倉垣，克之，神虎伐其功，徑還襄邑。

translations.literal: Linzi led Shenhu to attack Cangyuan and took it; Shenhu claimed the merit and went straight back to Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi led Shenhu in an attack on Cangyuan and took it, but Shenhu claimed the credit and went straight back to Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 林子軍次襄邑，即殺神虎而撫其眾。

translations.literal: When Linzi's army halted at Xiangyi, he immediately killed Shenhu and comforted his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Linzi's army halted at Xiangyi, he immediately executed Shenhu and reassured Shenhu's troops.

sentences.zh: 時偽建威將軍、河北太守薛帛先據解縣，林子至，馳往襲之，帛棄軍奔關中，林子收其兵糧。

translations.literal: At that time the false General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Hebei Xue Bo first held Jie county; when Linzi arrived he galloped to surprise him; Bo abandoned the army and fled to Guanzhong; Linzi collected his troops and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin general Xue Bo, titled General Who Establishes Might and Administrator of Hebei, held Jie county. When Linzi arrived he galloped to surprise him. Bo abandoned his army and fled to Guanzhong, and Linzi seized his troops and grain.

sentences.zh: 偽并州刺史、河東太守尹昭據蒲阪，林子於陝城與冠軍檀道濟同攻蒲阪，龍驤王鎮惡攻潼關。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Bing Province and Administrator of Hedong Yin Zhao held Puban; Linzi at Shaan city with Champion Tan Daoji jointly attacked Puban; Dragon Coursing Wang Zhen'e attacked Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Qin Inspector of Bing Province and Administrator of Hedong, Yin Zhao, held Puban. At Shaan city Linzi joined Champion Tan Daoji in attacking Puban, while Wang Zhen'e, Dragon Coursing General, assaulted Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚泓聞大軍至，遣偽東平公姚紹爭據潼關。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong heard the great army had arrived, he sent the false Duke of Dongping Yao Shao to contend for and hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong learned that the main army had arrived, he sent the Duke of Dongping, Yao Shao, to seize and hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 林子謂道濟曰：「今蒲阪城堅池深，不可旬日而克，攻之則士卒傷，守之則引日久，不如棄之，還援潼關。

translations.literal: Linzi said to Daoji: "Now Puban fortress is strong and moat deep— it cannot be taken in ten days; attacking will wound the soldiers; holding will prolong days— better abandon it and return to aid Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi said to Daoji, "Puban has strong walls and a deep moat. It cannot be taken in ten days. To attack will cost us soldiers; to besiege will waste time. Better abandon it and return to aid Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 且潼關天阻，所謂形勝之地，鎮惡孤軍，勢危力屈。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong Pass is a heavenly barrier, the so-called terrain of form and victory; Zhen'e's solitary army is in perilous straits with strength exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is a natural barrier, a classic strongpoint. Zhen'e's isolated force is in peril and near exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 若使姚紹據之，則難圖也。

translations.literal: If Yao Shao holds it, it will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If Yao Shao takes it, the pass will be hard to win.

sentences.zh: 及其未至，當並力爭之。

translations.literal: Before he arrives, we should combine strength to contend for it.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrives we must combine our forces and fight for it.

sentences.zh: 若潼關事捷，尹昭可不戰而服。

translations.literal: If Tong Pass succeeds, Yin Zhao can submit without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: If Tong Pass is taken, Yin Zhao will submit without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」道濟從之。

translations.literal: " Daoji followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 既至，紹舉關右之眾，設重圍圍林子及道濟、鎮惡等。

translations.literal: Having arrived, Shao mustered the forces of the Right of the Pass, set up a heavy encirclement around Linzi and Daoji, Zhen'e, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, Yao Shao rallied the armies of Guanxi and threw a tight cordon around Linzi, Tan Daoji, Wang Zhen'e, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 時懸師深入，糧輸艱遠，三軍疑阻，莫有固志。

translations.literal: At the time the army was deep in hostile territory; grain transport was arduous and distant; the three armies were doubtful and obstructed, and none had firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: The army was far inside enemy country, supplies were hard to bring up, and doubt spread through the ranks until no one held firm.

sentences.zh: 道濟議欲渡河避其鋒，或欲棄捐輜重，還赴高祖。

translations.literal: Daoji proposed crossing the river to avoid their edge; some wished to abandon baggage and return to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji argued for crossing the river to dodge the enemy's thrust; others wanted to dump the baggage train and march back to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 林子按劍曰：「相公勤王，志清六合，許、洛已平，關右將定，事之濟否，所系前鋒。

translations.literal: Linzi grasped his sword and said: "The Lord raised troops to aid the dynasty, intent on pacifying all under Heaven. Xu and Luo are already pacified; the Right of the Pass will soon be settled. Whether the affair succeeds depends on the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi hand on sword, said, "My lord took the field to restore the throne and clear the realm. Xu and Luoyang are already pacified; Guanxi will soon follow. Success or failure now hangs on the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 今舍已捷之形，棄垂成之業，大軍尚遠，賊眾方盛，雖欲求還，豈可複得。

translations.literal: Now to abandon a victorious posture and discard a nearly completed enterprise—the main army is still far, the rebel masses are at their peak— even if you wish to return, how could you again achieve it?
translations.idiomatic: To throw away a winning position and a victory almost in hand, with the main force still far off and the enemy at full strength— even if you wanted to retreat, how could you hope to get out?

sentences.zh: 下官受命前驅，誓在盡命，今日之事，自為將軍辦之。

translations.literal: This humble official received orders as advance guard, sworn to give my life. Today's affair I will handle for the General myself.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to lead the van and swore to spend my life in the effort. Leave today's fight to me, General—I will see it through.

sentences.zh: 然二三君子，或同業艱難，或荷恩罔極，以此退撓，亦何以見相公旗鼓耶！

translations.literal: Yet you gentlemen— some who shared hardships in the same enterprise, some who received boundless grace—to retreat and waver thus, how would you face the Lord's banners and drums!
translations.idiomatic: And you— some who marched through hardship together, some who owe him more than you can repay— if you shrink back now, how will you ever stand before his banners again?

sentences.zh: 」塞井焚舍，示無全志，率麾下數百人犯其西北。

translations.literal: " He blocked the wells and burned the quarters, showing no intent to preserve himself whole, and led several hundred men under his command to strike their northwest.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the wells and burned his camp to show he would not retreat whole, then led a few hundred men straight at the enemy's northwest flank.

sentences.zh: 紹眾小靡，乘其亂而薄之，紹乃大潰，俘虜以千數，悉獲紹器械資實。

translations.literal: Shao's masses slightly scattered; riding the disorder he pressed them close. Shao then completely routed; captives numbered in the thousands, and Shao's weapons and supplies were fully captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's line buckled; Linzi drove into the confusion and closed. Shao's army broke completely. Thousands were taken prisoner, along with all his arms and stores.

sentences.zh: 時諸將破賊，皆多其首級，而林子獻捷書至，每以實聞，高祖問其故，林子曰：「夫王者之師，本有征無戰，豈可複增張虛獲，以自誇誕。

translations.literal: At the time the generals defeating rebels all inflated head counts, but when Linzi's victory report arrived he always reported truthfully. Gaozu asked the reason. Linzi said: "A king's army by nature has campaigns without battles— how could one again inflate false gains to boast and exaggerate?
translations.idiomatic: Other generals padded their body counts, but Linzi's dispatches always gave the plain facts. When Gaozu asked why, Linzi said, "A true royal army wins by presence, not slaughter. How can we inflate false kills to puff ourselves up?

sentences.zh: 國淵以事實見賞，魏尚以盈級受罰，此亦前事之師表，後乘之良轍也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuan was rewarded for truth; Wei Shang was punished for excess counts— these are also models from past affairs, good tracks for those who follow.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuan was honored for telling the truth; Wei Shang was punished for padding his tally. Those are the precedents worth following.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「乃所望於卿也。」

translations.literal: " Gaozu said: "That is what I expected of you."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "That is exactly what I expect of you."

sentences.zh: 初，紹退走，還保定城，留偽武衛將軍姚鸞精兵守險。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shao retreated, he returned to Baoding city and left the false Military Guard General Yao Luan with elite troops holding the defiles.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao first fell back, he withdrew to Baoding and left the Qin general Yao Luan with picked troops holding the passes.

sentences.zh: 林子銜枚夜襲，即屠其城，劓鸞而坑其眾。

translations.literal: Linzi, with gags in mouths, made a night assault, immediately slaughtered the city, mutilated Luan's nose, and buried his troops alive in pits.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi struck at night with his men silenced by gags, stormed the city, cut off Luan's nose, and buried his soldiers alive.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜書曰：「頻再破賊，慶快無譬。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent a letter saying: "Repeatedly breaking the rebels— joy beyond comparison.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote, "You have broken the enemy again and again— my delight is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 既屢摧破，想不復久爾。

translations.literal: Having repeatedly crushed and broken them, I suppose it will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: With so many defeats behind them, I doubt this can last much longer.

sentences.zh: 」紹複遣撫軍將軍姚贊將兵屯河上，絕水道。

translations.literal: " Shao again sent Pacification Army General Yao Zan to lead troops encamped on the river, cutting off the water route.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Pacification Army General Yao Zan to camp on the river and cut the water supply.

sentences.zh: 贊壘塹未立，林子邀擊，連破之，贊輕騎得脫，眾皆奔敗。

translations.literal: Before Zan's ramparts and ditches were established, Linzi intercepted and attacked, successively broke them. Zan escaped with light cavalry; the masses all fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zan could finish his fortifications, Linzi hit him, broke him again and again, and Zan escaped with a handful of horsemen while the rest scattered.

sentences.zh: 紹又遣長史領軍將軍姚伯子、甯朔將軍安鸞、護軍姚默騾、平遠將軍河東太守唐小方率眾三萬，屯據九泉，憑河固險，以絕糧援。

translations.literal: Shao again sent Chief Administrator and Army-leader General Yao Bozi, Pacifying the North General An Luan, Protector of the Army Yao Mozhen, Pacifying the Distant General and Hedong Administrator Tang Xiaofang leading thirty thousand men, encamped at Jiuquan, relying on the river to secure the defiles, to cut off grain relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sent Chief Administrator Yao Bozi, Ningshuo General An Luan, Protector of the Army Yao Mozhen, and Pacifying-the-Distant General and Hedong Administrator Tang Xiaofang with thirty thousand men to hold Jiuquan on the river, fortify the crossing, and block grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 高祖以通津阻要，兵糧所急，複遣林子爭據河源。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because the ford was strategically critical and military grain urgent, again sent Linzi to contest and seize the river source.
translations.idiomatic: The ford was vital and supplies were running short, so Gaozu sent Linzi back to fight for control of the riverhead.

sentences.zh: 林子率太尉行參軍嚴綱、竺靈秀卷甲進討，累戰，大破之，即斬伯子、默騾、小方三級，所俘馘及驢馬器械甚多。

translations.literal: Linzi led Grand Marshal Acting Army Aide Yan Gang and Zhu Lingxiu with armor rolled up, advancing to attack; fought repeatedly and greatly defeated them, immediately beheading the three ranks Bozi, Mozhen, and Xiaofang. Captives, severed heads, donkeys, horses, and weapons were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi marched with Yan Gang and Zhu Lingxiu, armor on and no time wasted, and after a series of battles routed the enemy, beheading Bozi, Mozhen, and Xiaofang. The haul of prisoners, heads, pack animals, and arms was enormous.

sentences.zh: 所虜獲三千餘人，悉以還紹，使知王師之弘。

translations.literal: Captives taken numbered over three thousand; all were returned to Shao, to let him know the royal army's magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: More than three thousand captives were sent back to Shao unharmed, a gesture meant to show the imperial army's clemency.

sentences.zh: 兵糧兼儲，三軍鼓行而西矣。

translations.literal: Military grain was doubly stored; the three armies marched with drums beating westward.
translations.idiomatic: With grain stocked in abundance, the whole army beat drums and marched west.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「彼去國遠鬥，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Someone said: "They fight far from their homeland; their edge cannot be withstood."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "They are fighting far from home— their momentum is unstoppable."

sentences.zh: 」林子白高祖曰：「姚紹氣蓋關右，而力以勢屈，外兵屢敗，衰亡協兆，但恐凶命先盡，不得以釁齊斧爾。

translations.literal: " Linzi reported to Gaozu: "Yao Shao's spirit covers the Right of the Pass, yet his strength is bent by circumstance. External armies have repeatedly been defeated; signs of decline and extinction coalesce. I only fear his wicked fate will end first, and he will not meet the executioner's axe.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi wrote Gaozu, "Yao Shao still dominates Guanxi in name, but his power is already broken. His allies keep losing. Every sign points to collapse. I only worry he will die before we can bring him to justice.

sentences.zh: 」尋紹忽死，可謂天誅。

translations.literal: " Soon after, Shao suddenly died— it could be called heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Shao died suddenly— heaven's judgment, one might say.

sentences.zh: 於是贊統後事，鳩集餘眾，複襲林子。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zan took over subsequent affairs, gathered the remaining masses, and again attacked Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zan took command, rallied the survivors, and came at Linzi again.

sentences.zh: 林子率師禦之，旗鼓未交，一時披潰，贊輕騎遁走。

translations.literal: Linzi led the army to resist. Before banners and drums met, they instantly scattered and routed; Zan fled on light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi met him head-on. Before the lines even clashed, the enemy broke and ran; Zan escaped with a few riders.

sentences.zh: 既連戰皆捷，士馬旌旗甚盛，高祖賜書勸勉，並致縑帛肴漿。

translations.literal: Having connected victories, soldiers, horses, banners, and drums were very flourishing. Gaozu sent a letter encouraging him and also sent silk cloth, meat, and broth.
translations.idiomatic: Victory followed victory, and Linzi's camp swelled with men, horses, and banners. Gaozu wrote to praise him and sent silk, meat, and wine.

sentences.zh: 高祖至閿鄉，姚泓掃境內之民，屯兵堯柳。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached Wen Township, Yao Hong swept the people within the borders and massed troops at Yao Willow.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu reached Wen Township, Yao Hong emptied the countryside and massed his army at Yao Willow.

sentences.zh: 時田子自武關北入，屯軍藍田，泓自率大眾攻之。

translations.literal: At the time Tianzi entered from the north via Wu Pass and encamped at Lantian; Hong personally led the main force to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tianzi had come down from Wu Pass and was camped at Lantian when Hong marched out in person to attack him.

sentences.zh: 高祖慮眾寡不敵，遣林子步自秦嶺，以相接援。

translations.literal: Gaozu feared the many could not match the few and sent Linzi by foot from Qin Ridge to connect and reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Tianzi was outnumbered, Gaozu sent Linzi over the Qin Mountains on foot to link up and reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 比至，泓已摧破，兄弟複共追討，泓乃舉眾奔霸西。

translations.literal: By the time he arrived, Hong had already been shattered and broken. The brothers together again pursued; Hong then raised the masses and fled to Ba West.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Linzi arrived, Hong was already beaten. The two brothers pressed the pursuit together, and Hong fled west of Ba with what was left of his force.

sentences.zh: 田子欲窮追，進取長安，林子止之，曰：「往取長安，如指掌爾。

translations.literal: Tianzi wanted to pursue to the end, advance, and take Chang'an. Linzi stopped him, saying: "To go take Chang'an is like reading one's palm.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi wanted to run Hong down and seize Chang'an. Linzi stopped him. "Chang'an is within our grasp—

sentences.zh: 複克賊城，便為獨平一國，不賞之功也。

translations.literal: Again capturing rebel cities would be a merit of pacifying a state alone— an un-rewardable achievement.
translations.idiomatic: but if you take it now, you alone will have pacified a kingdom. That is a feat too great to reward."

sentences.zh: 」田子乃止。

translations.literal: " Tianzi then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi held back.

sentences.zh: 復參相國事，總任如前。

translations.literal: He again participated in grand counselor affairs; overall responsibilities were as before.
translations.idiomatic: He resumed his role in the chief minister's council with the same broad authority as before.

sentences.zh: 林子威聲遠聞，三輔震動，關中豪右，望風請附。

translations.literal: Linzi's prestige and fame were heard afar; the Three Adjuncts trembled; powerful families of Guanzhong, at the wind, requested to attach.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi's name carried far. The Three Adjuncts shook, and the great families of Guanzhong came over at the first rumor of his approach.

sentences.zh: 西州人李焉等並求立功，孫妲羌雜夷及姚泓親屬，盡相率歸林子。

translations.literal: Western region people Li Yan and others all sought to establish merit; Sun Da, Qiang, and mixed Yi barbarians, and Yao Hong's kin, all in succession submitted to Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Li Yan of the western provinces offered their service; Sun clansmen, Qiang, mixed tribes, and even Yao Hong's own kin turned to Linzi one after another.

sentences.zh: 高祖以林子綏略有方，頻賜書褒美，並令深慰納之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because Linzi's pacifying and planning had method, frequently sent letters praising him and also ordered deep consolation and acceptance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised Linzi's steady hand in winning people over and told him to treat every defector with care.

sentences.zh: 長安既平，殘羌十餘萬口，西奔隴上，林子追討至寡婦水，轉鬥達於槐里，克之，俘獲萬計。

translations.literal: After Chang'an was pacified, remnant Qiang over a hundred thousand mouths fled west to Longshang. Linzi pursued to Widow's Water, turned and fought reaching Huaili, captured it, and captives numbered in the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell, more than a hundred thousand Qiang fled west into Longshang. Linzi chased them to Widow's Water, fought his way to Huaili, took the city, and captured tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 大軍東歸，林子領水軍于石門，以為聲援。

translations.literal: The main army returned east; Linzi led the navy at Shimen as vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force marched east, Linzi took the river fleet to Shimen to cover the withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 還至郡，高祖器其才智，不使出也。

translations.literal: Returning to the commandery, Gaozu valued his wisdom and talent and did not let him go out.
translations.idiomatic: Back at headquarters, Gaozu prized his mind too highly to send him away again.

sentences.zh: 故出仕以來，便管軍要，自非戎軍所指，未嘗外典焉。

translations.literal: Thus from entering office he then managed military essentials; except where the military campaign pointed, he never externally administered.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he entered service he held the army's core portfolios and was never posted outside except on campaign.

sentences.zh: 後太祖出鎮荊州，議以林子及謝晦為蕃佐，高祖曰：「吾不可頓無二人，林子行則晦不宜出。

translations.literal: Later Taizu went out to guard Jingzhou. They discussed taking Linzi and Xie Hui as frontier assistants. Gaozu said: "I cannot suddenly be without both men. If Linzi goes, then Hui should not go out.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu was sent to guard Jingzhou, the court considered posting Linzi and Xie Hui as his deputies. Gaozu said, "I cannot lose both at once. If Linzi goes, Hui must stay.

sentences.zh: 」乃以林子為西郎中兵參軍，領新興太守。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Linzi was made Western Central Commandant Army Aide, concurrently Xinxing Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi was made Western Central Commandant Army Aide and Administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 林子思議弘深，有所陳畫，高祖未嘗不稱善。

translations.literal: Linzi's thought and deliberation were broad and deep; whatever he presented and planned, Gaozu never failed to praise as good.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi's counsel ran deep, and Gaozu never heard a proposal from him he did not approve.

sentences.zh: 大軍還至彭城，林子以行役既久，士有歸心，深陳事宜，並言：「聖王所以戒慎祗肅，非以崇威立武，實乃經國長民，宜廣建蕃屏，崇嚴宿衛。

translations.literal: When the main army returned to Pengcheng, Linzi, because the campaign had lasted long and soldiers had thoughts of return, deeply stated the affairs and also said: "The sage king's reason for vigilance and reverence is not to exalt awe and establish martial power— truly it is to govern the state and nurture the people. One should broadly establish feudal screens and elevate and strengthen guard detachments.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned to Pengcheng, Linzi— noting how long the men had been in the field and how eager they were to go home— laid out his concerns and said, "A sage ruler's vigilance is not about posturing with arms. It is about governing the realm and caring for the people. We should strengthen the feudal shields around the throne and tighten the guard at court.

sentences.zh: 」高祖深相訓納。

translations.literal: " Gaozu deeply accepted and followed the instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 俄而謝翼謀反，高祖歎曰：「林子之見，何其明也。

translations.literal: Soon Xie Yi plotted rebellion. Gaozu sighed: "Linzi's insight— how bright it was!
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Yi soon after rose in rebellion, Gaozu sighed, "Linzi saw it coming— how sharp he was!

sentences.zh: 」太祖進號鎮西，隨府轉，加建威將軍、河東太守。

translations.literal: " Taizu advanced in title to Pacifier of the West, followed the headquarters in transfer, and was added Jianwei General and Hedong Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was promoted to Pacifier of the West; Linzi moved with his staff and was given the additional titles of Jianwei General and Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時高祖以二虜侵擾，複欲親戎，林子固諫，高祖答曰：「吾輒當不復自行。」

translations.literal: At the time Gaozu, because the two barbarians harried and disturbed, again wanted to personally take the field. Linzi firmly remonstrated. Gaozu replied: "I for my part shall not again go out myself."
translations.idiomatic: When the northern enemies pressed again, Gaozu wanted to take the field in person. Linzi argued hard against it. Gaozu answered, "Very well—I will not lead another campaign myself."

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，以佐命功，封漢壽縣伯，食邑六百戶，固讓，不許。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, for assisting-establishment merit he enfeoffed Linzi as Marquis of Hanshou with six hundred households. Linzi firmly declined; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu's accession, Linzi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hanshou with six hundred households for his role in founding the dynasty. He tried to refuse; the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 傅亮與林子書曰：「班爵疇勳，歷代常典，封賞之發，簡自帝心。

translations.literal: Fu Liang wrote to Linzi: "Enfeoffing ranks and arranging merit is the constant canon of successive generations; the issuing of fiefs and rewards is selected from the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Liang wrote Linzi, "Granting rank and sorting merit by deed is the way of every dynasty. Honors come straight from the throne.

sentences.zh: 主上委寄之懷，實參休否，誠心所期，同國榮戚，政複是卿諸人共弘建內外爾。

translations.literal: The sovereign's entrusting sentiment truly participates in fortune and misfortune; the sincerity one hopes for, sharing the state's glory and sorrow— is indeed for you gentlemen together to broadly establish inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stakes his trust in you because your fates are bound to the realm's. What he asks is that you and your peers strengthen the court at home and abroad together.

sentences.zh: 足下雖存挹退，豈得獨為君子邪！

translations.literal: Though you preserve yielding restraint, how can you alone be a gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: You may be modest, but you cannot be the only man who refuses his due!"

sentences.zh: 」除府諮議參軍，將軍、太守如故。

translations.literal: He was appointed headquarters Advisory Army Aide; his generalship and administrator post remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Advisory Army Aide on the prince's staff while keeping his generalship and prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋召暫下，以中兵局事副錄事參軍王華。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned temporarily down; central military bureau affairs were deputized to Recording Army Aide Wang Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called away on leave, and Wang Hua took over the central military desk in his stead.

sentences.zh: 上以林子清公勤儉，賞賜重疊，皆散於親故。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Linzi was pure, fair, diligent, and frugal, piled up rewards and gifts— all were dispersed to kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heaped gifts on Linzi for his integrity and thrift; Linzi gave every one away to relatives and old friends.

sentences.zh: 家無餘財，未嘗問生產之事，中表孤貧悉歸焉。

translations.literal: The household had no surplus wealth; he never inquired into production affairs; cousins and relatives who were orphaned and poor all came to him.
translations.idiomatic: His house held nothing extra. He never fussed over income. Every poor cousin and orphaned relative found shelter with him.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，還東葬，乘輿躬幸，信使相望。

translations.literal: Encountering his mother's mourning, he returned east to bury her. The imperial carriage personally attended; messengers of trust came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he went east to bury her. The emperor came in person, and couriers bearing the throne's condolences never stopped coming.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，詔曰：「軍國多務，內外須才，前鎮西諮議、建威將軍、河東太守沈林子，不得遂其情事，可起輔國將軍。

translations.literal: After the burial, an edict said: "Military and state have many affairs; inside and outside need talent. Former Pacifier of the West Advisory Aide, Jianwei General, and Hedong Administrator Shen Linzi cannot follow his sentiment in affairs; he may rise as Assistant General.
translations.idiomatic: After the funeral an edict ran, "State and army both need able men. Former Pacifier of the West Advisory Aide, Jianwei General, and Hedong Administrator Shen Linzi may not remain in mourning— recall him as Assistant General.

sentences.zh: 」林子固辭，不許，賜墨詔，朔望不復還朝，每軍國大事，輒詢問焉。

translations.literal: " Linzi firmly declined; it was not permitted. He was granted an ink edict; on the first and fifteenth he no longer returned to court. Whenever major military and state affairs arose, he was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi begged off again and was refused. By special edict he was excused from the first- and fifteenth-day audiences, but on every weighty matter the throne sought his word.

sentences.zh: 時領軍將軍謝晦任當國政，晦每疾寧，輒攝林子代之。

translations.literal: At the time Army-leader General Xie Hui held national government. Whenever Hui fell ill and rested, Linzi was deputized to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Army-leader General Xie Hui ran the government; whenever illness kept Hui away, Linzi stood in for him.

sentences.zh: 林子居喪至孝，高祖深相憂湣。

translations.literal: Linzi in mourning was utmost filial; Gaozu deeply sympathized and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi mourned with fierce devotion, and Gaozu grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 頃之有疾，上以林子孝性，不欲使哭泣減損，逼與入省，日夕撫慰。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill. The emperor, because of Linzi's filial nature, did not wish to let weeping reduce his health, pressed him to enter the inner palace, and day and night comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell sick. Fearing grief would waste him, the emperor had him brought into the palace and watched over him day and night.

sentences.zh: 敕諸公曰：「其至性過人，卿等數慰視之。

translations.literal: An edict to the lords said: "His utmost nature surpasses others— you should several times visit and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the ministers, "His devotion is extraordinary— go often and comfort him.

sentences.zh: 」小差乃出。

translations.literal: " When slightly recovered, he then went out.
translations.idiomatic: When he improved a little, he was allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 上尋不豫，被敕入侍醫藥，會疾動還外。

translations.literal: The emperor soon fell ill and ordered him to enter and attend with medicine. When the illness stirred, he returned outside.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor himself sickened, Linzi was summoned to tend him. When the sickness worsened, he was sent home again.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，薨，時年四十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died, age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he died, at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 群公知上深相矜重，恐以實啟，必有損慟，每見呼問，輒答疾病還家，或有中旨，亦假為其答。

translations.literal: The lords, knowing the emperor deeply cherished and valued him, feared reporting the truth would certainly bring excessive grief. Whenever summoned and asked, they answered that he was ill and had returned home; or if there was an imperial order, they also falsely answered for him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers, knowing how dear Linzi was to the emperor, hid the truth lest the shock kill him. When Gaozu asked after Linzi, they said he was ill at home; even imperial messages were answered with lies.

sentences.zh: 高祖尋崩，竟不知也。

translations.literal: Gaozu soon died; in the end Linzi did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu died soon after— never knowing Linzi was already gone.

sentences.zh: 賜東園秘器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: Linzi was granted the Eastern Garden secret coffin, one set of court dress, one suit of clothes, two hundred thousand coins, and two hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him the imperial coffin from the Eastern Garden, a full set of court robes, another suit of clothes, two hundred thousand cash, and two hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「故輔國將軍沈林子，器懷真審，忠績允著，才志未遂，傷悼在懷。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Former Assistant General Shen Linzi— capacity and mind truly sincere, loyalty and achievement clearly evident, talents and ambitions not yet fulfilled— sorrow lodges in the breast.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Former Assistant General Shen Linzi was honest in heart and steadfast in deed. His talent had not yet reached its limit, and the grief of his loss weighs on us.

sentences.zh: 可追贈征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously enfeoffed as General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 」有司率常典也。

translations.literal: " The relevant offices followed the regular canon.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries carried out the rites as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十五年，諡曰懷伯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Yuanjia, his posthumous title was Huai Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia twenty-five he was given the posthumous title Marquis Huai.

sentences.zh: 林子簡泰廉靖，不交接世務，義讓之美，著於閨門，雖在戎旅，語不及軍事。

translations.literal: Linzi was simple, composed, honest, and tranquil; he did not mix in worldly affairs. The beauty of righteousness and yielding was renowned within the inner chambers. Though in military camp, speech did not touch military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi was spare, quiet, and upright. He kept out of worldly entanglements; at home he was known for courtesy and restraint. Even in camp he rarely spoke of war.

sentences.zh: 所著詩、賦、贊、三言、箴、祭文、樂府、表、箋、書記、白事、啟事、論、老子一百二十一首。

translations.literal: His writings— poems, fu, encomia, three-character texts, admonitions, sacrificial texts, yuefu, memorials, letters of presentation, letters, white reports, reports, disquisitions, and Laozi— numbered one hundred twenty-one pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left 121 works: poems, rhapsodies, encomia, three-character verse, admonitions, sacrificial texts, yuefu songs, memorials, letters, reports, essays, and a commentary on the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 太祖後讀林子集，歎息曰：「此人作公，應繼王太保。

translations.literal: Later Taizu read Linzi's collected works and sighed: "If this man became a public minister, he should succeed Grand Guardian Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, reading Linzi's collected writings, Taizu sighed, "Had this man served in civil office, he would have been Wang Dao's heir.

sentences.zh: 」子邵嗣。

translations.literal: " His son Shao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 劭，字道輝，美風姿，涉獵文史。

translations.literal: Shao, styled Daohui, had handsome bearing and widely read literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, courtesy name Daohui, was handsome and well read in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，駙馬都尉、奉朝請。

translations.literal: He inherited the fief, Attendant Cavalry Commandant, and attendant at court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the marquisate, served as Attendant Cavalry Commandant, and attended court.

sentences.zh: 太祖以舊恩召見，入拜，便流涕，太祖亦悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Taizu, because of old grace, summoned him to an audience. Entering to bow, he then wept; Taizu also could not restrain grief.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, remembering old ties, summoned him. Shao entered, bowed, and wept; Taizu could not keep his composure either.

sentences.zh: 會強弩將軍缺，上詔錄尚書彭城王義康曰：「沈邵人身不惡，吾與林子周旋異常，可以補選。

translations.literal: When the Strong Crossbow General post was vacant, the emperor ordered to record for Prince of Pengcheng Yikang: "Shen Shao's person is not bad. I associated with Linzi exceptionally; he can fill the selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Strong Crossbow General fell open, the emperor told Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, "Shen Shao is a good man. I was close to his father— put him forward.

sentences.zh: 」事見宋文帝中詔於是拜強弩將軍。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the middle edicts of Emperor Wen of Song." Thereupon Shao was appointed Strong Crossbow General.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is noted among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts." Shao was then made Strong Crossbow General.

sentences.zh: 出為鐘離太守，在郡有惠政，夾淮人民慕其化，遠近莫不投集。

translations.literal: He went out as Zhongli Administrator. In the commandery he had benevolent governance; people on both sides of the Huai admired his transformation, and near and far none did not submit and gather.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Zhongli. His rule was humane, and people on both banks of the Huai came to him from far and near.

sentences.zh: 郡先無市，時江夏王義恭為南兗州，啟太祖置立焉事見宋文帝中詔。

translations.literal: The commandery previously had no market. At the time Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was Southern Yanzhou and memorialized Taizu to establish one. The affair is recorded in the middle edicts of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The district had never had a market. Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, then governor of Southern Yanzhou, asked Taizu to authorize one— also recorded among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts.

sentences.zh: 義恭又啟太祖曰：「盱眙太守劉顯真求自解說，邵往蒞任有績，彰於民聽，若重授盱眙，足為良二千石。

translations.literal: Yigong again memorialized Taizu: "Xuyi Administrator Liu Xianzhen requests to resign and explain. Shao, going to take the appointment, has achievement clear in popular hearing. If again appointing Xuyi, he would be sufficient as a good two-thousand-bushel official.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong wrote again, "Xuyi Administrator Liu Xianzhen asks to be relieved. Shao has done well at Zhongli and is well spoken of. If you move him to Xuyi, he will make a fine prefect.

sentences.zh: 」上不許，曰：「其願還經年，方復作此流遷，必當大罔罔也。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not permit, saying: "His wish to return has been years. Just again making this kind of transfer, he would certainly become very dazed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused. "He has wanted to come back for years. Shuffle him around like this and he will only grow more lost.

sentences.zh: 」事見宋文帝中詔。

translations.literal: The affair is recorded in the middle edicts of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: That too is recorded among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts.

sentences.zh: 上敕州辟邵弟亮，邵以從弟正蚤孤，乞移恩於正，上嘉而許之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the province to recruit Shao's younger brother Liang. Shao, because his junior cousin Zheng was early orphaned, begged to shift grace to Zheng; the emperor praised and permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered the province to recruit Shao's brother Liang. Shao asked that the favor go instead to his orphaned cousin Zheng; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 在任六年，入為衡陽王義季右軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: In office six years, he entered as Right Army Central Military Aide to Prince of Hengyang Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in the prefecture he returned as Right Army Central Military Aide to Prince of Hengyang Yiji.

sentences.zh: 始興王浚初開後軍府，又為中兵。

translations.literal: When Prince of Shixing Jun first opened the Rear Army headquarters, Shao again served as central military aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Shixing Jun first opened his Rear Army headquarters, Shao again served as central military aide.

sentences.zh: 義季在江陵，安西府中兵久缺，啟太祖求人，上答曰：「稱意才難得。

translations.literal: Yiji was at Jiangling; the Anxi headquarters central military aide had long been vacant. He memorialized Taizu seeking a person. The emperor replied: "Satisfactory talent is hard to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji was at Jiangling with no central military aide for the Anxi command. He asked Taizu for a man. The emperor answered, "Good men are hard to find.

sentences.zh: 沈邵雖未經軍事，既是腹心，作鐘離郡，及在後軍府，房中甚修理，或欲遣之。

translations.literal: Shen Shao, though never having undergone military affairs, is already a trusted confidant. He served as Zhongli commandery and, in the rear army headquarters, inner chambers were very well maintained. Perhaps one wishes to send him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shao has no battlefield experience, but he is trusted inner circle. He ran Zhongli well and keeps the rear army household in good order. I may send him.

sentences.zh: 」其事不果事見宋文帝中詔。

translations.literal: " That affair did not come to fruition. The matter is recorded in the middle edicts of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not go— again noted among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts.

sentences.zh: 入為通直郎。

translations.literal: He entered as Direct Communication Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Direct Communication Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時上多行幸，還或侵夜，邵啟事陳論，即為簡出。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor often went on tours; returning sometimes encroached on night. Shao's reports and memorials stated arguments and were immediately selected and issued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled often and sometimes returned late at night. Shao's memorials laid out the issues plainly and were promptly approved and sent out.

sentences.zh: 前後密陳政要，上皆納用之，深相寵待，晨夕兼侍，每出遊，或敕同輦。

translations.literal: Before and after, he secretly submitted important policy matters; the emperor all adopted and used them, deeply favored and treated him, morning and evening both attending, every time going out on tour, sometimes ordered [him] to ride in the same carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly submitted confidential policy briefs, and the emperor adopted every one. Deeply favored, Shao attended him morning and night; on outings the emperor sometimes ordered him to share the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 時車駕祀南郊，特詔邵兼侍中負璽，代真官陪乘。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage sacrificed at the Southern Suburb, specially ordered Shao concurrently Attendant Within to carry the seal, replacing the proper official as accompanying rider.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the Southern Suburb sacrifice, he specially ordered Shao to serve concurrently as Attendant Within, bearing the imperial seal in place of the regular officer on the accompaniment carriage.

sentences.zh: 大將軍彭城王義康出鎮豫章，申謨為中兵參軍，掌城防之任，廬陵王紹為江州，以邵為南中郎府錄事參軍，行府州事，事未行，會謨丁艱，邵代謨為大將軍中兵，加寧朔將軍事見宋文帝中詔。

translations.literal: Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang went out to garrison Yuzhang; Shen Mo served as Central Military Aide, in charge of the duty of city defense. Prince of Luling Shao became Jiang Province; Shao was appointed Southern Central Commandant headquarters Recorder-Aide, acting on headquarters and province affairs. The matter had not yet been carried out when Mo encountered mourning for a parent; Shao replaced Mo as the Grand General's central military aide, with added Ningshuo General— the affair is recorded in the middle edicts of Emperor Wen of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang went to Yuzhang, Shen Mo was central military aide in charge of the city's defenses. When Prince of Luling Shao took Jiang Province, Shao was made recorder-aide of the Southern Central Commandant headquarters to handle its provincial affairs. Before he could leave, Mo entered mourning; Shao replaced him as the grand general's central military aide with the rank of Ningshuo General— noted among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts.

sentences.zh: 邵南行，上遂相任委，不復選代，仍兼錄事，領城局。

translations.literal: Shao went south; the emperor then entrusted him, no longer selecting a replacement, still concurrently recorder, overseeing the city bureau.
translations.idiomatic: As Shao headed south, the emperor entrusted him fully, appointed no successor, and kept him as recorder in charge of the city bureau.

sentences.zh: 後義康被廢，邵改為廬陵王紹南中郎參軍，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Later Yikang was deposed; Shao was changed to Southern Central Commandant Aide to Prince of Luling Shao; his generalship remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Yikang's fall, Shao was reassigned as Southern Central Commandant Aide to Prince of Luling Shao, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 義康徙安成，邵複以本號為安成相。

translations.literal: Yikang was moved to Ancheng; Shao again, with his original title, became Ancheng Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yikang was exiled to Ancheng, Shao was made chancellor of Ancheng under the same title.

sentences.zh: 在郡以寬和恩信，為南土所懷。

translations.literal: In the commandery, with lenience, harmony, grace, and trustworthiness, he was embraced by the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture he ruled with leniency and good faith, and the south held him in affection.

sentences.zh: 郡民王孚有學業，志行見稱州里，邵蒞任未幾，而孚卒，邵贈以孝廉，板教曰：「前文學主簿王孚，行潔業淳，棄華息競，志學修道，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: A commandery resident, Wang Fu, had learning and achievement; his will and conduct were praised in the district. Shao had not been long in office when Fu died. Shao honored him with Filial and Incorrupt [status], and a draft instruction said: "Former Literary Master of Records Wang Fu— conduct pure, achievement sincere, abandoned flourish and ceased rivalry, resolved to learn and cultivate the Way, old yet ever more steadfast.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu, a learned man of the district known for his character, died soon after Shao took office. Shao posthumously named him Filial and Incorrupt and drafted an instruction: "Former literary master of records Wang Fu lived purely and studied the Way without vanity or rivalry; in old age his devotion only deepened.

sentences.zh: 方授右職，不幸暴亡，可假孝廉檄，薦以特牲。

translations.literal: Just about to receive a right-side post, unluckily died suddenly; he may be granted a Filial and Incorrupt dispatch, recommended with a special sacrificial victim.
translations.idiomatic: He was on the verge of appointment when he died suddenly. Grant him a filial-and-incorrupt dispatch and recommend him with a special sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 緬想延陵，以遂本懷。

translations.literal: Longingly recalling Yanling, to fulfill his original aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling Yanling, we grant what his heart desired.

sentences.zh: 」邵慰恤孤老，勸課農桑，前後累蒙賞賜。

translations.literal: " Shao comforted and cared for orphans and elderly, urged and assessed farming and sericulture; before and after repeatedly received rewards and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shao comforted the orphaned and aged, promoted farming and silkworms, and was rewarded again and again.

sentences.zh: 邵疾病，使命累續，遣御醫上藥，異味遠珍，金帛衣裘，相望不絕。

translations.literal: Shao fell ill; imperial messengers came in succession, sending imperial physicians and superior medicines, exotic flavors and distant delicacies, gold, silk, clothing, and fur— one after another without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao fell ill, imperial couriers arrived in succession with court physicians, fine medicines, rare foods, gold, silk, and furs without end.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十六年，卒，時年四十三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Yuanjia, he died; at the time age forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 26 he died at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 上甚相痛悼。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly grieved and mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 子侃嗣，官至山陽王休祐驃騎中兵參軍、南沛郡太守。

translations.literal: His son Kan succeeded; office reached Central Military Aide to the Rapid Cavalry General of Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou, Administrator of Nanpei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kan inherited the fief and rose to central military aide to Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou's Rapid Cavalry command and Administrator of Nanpei.

sentences.zh: 侃卒，子整應襲爵，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: Kan died; his son Zheng should have inherited the fief; when Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After Kan died, his son Zheng would have inherited the marquisate, but when Qi took the throne the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 璞，字道真，林子少子也。

translations.literal: Pu, styled Daozhen, was Linzi's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, courtesy name Daozhen, was Linzi's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 童孺時，神意閑審，有異於眾。

translations.literal: In childhood years, his spirit and intent were leisurely and careful, different from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy his composure was unusual.

sentences.zh: 太祖問林子：「聞君小兒器質不凡，甚欲相識。

translations.literal: Taizu asked Linzi: "I hear your young son's capacity and quality are not ordinary; I very much wish to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked Linzi, "I hear your son is no ordinary boy. I should like to meet him.

sentences.zh: 」林子令璞進見，太祖奇璞應對，謂林子曰：「此非常兒。

translations.literal: " Linzi had Pu advance for an audience. Taizu marveled at Pu's responses and said to Linzi: "This is no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Linzi brought Pu in. Taizu was struck by his answers and told Linzi, "This is no ordinary child.

sentences.zh: 」年十許歲，智度便有大成之姿，好學不倦，善屬文，時有憶識之功。

translations.literal: " At about ten years, his wisdom and measure already had the bearing of great accomplishment; he loved learning without weariness, was skilled at composing prose, and at times had the power of memory and recollection.
translations.idiomatic: By ten he already showed great promise, studied tirelessly, wrote well, and had a remarkable memory.

sentences.zh: 尤練究萬事，經耳過目，人莫能欺之。

translations.literal: Especially practiced and investigated all matters; passed through the ear and eye— no one could deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered every detail; what reached his ear or eye could not be used to fool him.

sentences.zh: 居家精理，姻族資賴。

translations.literal: At home he meticulously managed affairs; kin and clan relied on his resources.
translations.idiomatic: At home he managed affairs with precision, and kin relied on him.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，吳興太守王韶之再命，不就。

translations.literal: At capped age, Wuxing Administrator Wang Shaozhi twice summoned him; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Wang Shaozhi, Administrator of Wuxing, summoned him twice; he declined both times.

sentences.zh: 張邵臨郡，又命為主簿，除南平王左常侍。

translations.literal: Zhang Shao came to the commandery and again appointed him Master of Records; he was appointed Left Regular Attendant to Prince of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shao took the prefecture he made Pu his master of records and then appointed him Left Regular Attendant to Prince of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 太祖引見，謂曰：「吾昔以弱年出蕃，卿家以親要見輔，今日之授，意在不薄。

translations.literal: Taizu summoned him for an audience and said: "I once, in tender years, went out to a fiefdom; your house, as close and important, was seen and aided. Today's appointment— the intent is not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu received him and said, "When I was young and went out to my fief, your family stood by me as trusted kin. This appointment is meant to be no small honor.

sentences.zh: 王家之事，一以相委，勿以國官乖清塗為罔罔也。」

translations.literal: Matters of the princely house— entirely entrusted to you. Do not, because state office diverges from the pure path, become dazed and confused."
translations.idiomatic: I leave princely affairs entirely to you. Do not let official rank distract you from the proper course."

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，始興王浚為揚州刺史，寵愛殊異，以為主簿。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia, Prince of Shixing Jun was Yang Province Inspector; favor and love were exceptionally different; Pu was made Master of Records.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 17 Prince of Shixing Jun became governor of Yang Province and favored Pu so greatly that he made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時順陽范曄為長史，行州事。

translations.literal: At the time Fan Ye of Shunyang was Chief Clerk, acting on province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye of Shunyang served as chief clerk and handled provincial business.

sentences.zh: 曄性頗疏，太祖召璞謂曰：「神畿之政，既不易理。

translations.literal: Ye's nature was rather careless. Taizu summoned Pu and said: "The governance of the divine capital region is already not easy to manage.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was slack by nature. Taizu called Pu in and said, "Running the imperial capital is hard enough.

sentences.zh: 浚以弱年臨州，萬物皆屬耳目，賞罰得失，特宜詳慎。

translations.literal: Jun, in tender years, oversees the province; all things belong to eye and ear; rewards, punishments, gains, and losses— especially should be detailed and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Jun is young; everything in the province reaches his ears. Rewards and punishments must be weighed with care.

sentences.zh: 范曄性疏，必多不同。

translations.literal: Fan Ye's nature is careless; there will certainly be much disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ye's lax habits will lead to friction.

sentences.zh: 卿腹心所寄，當密以在意。

translations.literal: You are the entrusted confidant; you should secretly keep this in mind.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on you as my eyes and ears— keep this in mind and report in confidence.

sentences.zh: 彼雖行事，其實委卿也。

translations.literal: Though he handles affairs, in fact he entrusts them to you.
translations.idiomatic: He may sign the orders, but the real authority is yours.

sentences.zh: 」璞以任遇既深，乃夙夜匪懈，其有所懷，輒以密啟，每至施行，必從中出。

translations.literal: " Because Pu's appointment and favor were already deep, he then morning and night without slackness; when he had something in mind, he at once secretly reported; whenever implementation came, it necessarily issued from the center.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply entrusted, Pu worked tirelessly. Whatever troubled him he reported secretly, and orders went out only through the center.

sentences.zh: 曄正謂聖明留察，故深更恭慎，而莫見其際也。

translations.literal: Ye just thought the sage clarity remained in observation; therefore he became deeply more respectful and careful, yet none saw its inner edge.
translations.idiomatic: Ye assumed the throne was watching closely and grew more deferential, never guessing Pu's role.

sentences.zh: 在職八年，神州大治，民無謗黷，璞有力焉。

translations.literal: In office eight years, the divine land was greatly ordered; the people had no slander or disrespect— Pu had strength in this.
translations.idiomatic: In eight years the capital was well governed and the people quiet— Pu had much to do with it.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，范曄坐事誅，于時浚雖曰親覽，州事一以付璞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Fan Ye, owing to an affair, was executed. At that time Jun, though said to inspect personally, all province affairs were given entirely to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 22 Fan Ye was executed for his crimes. Though Jun was nominally in charge, he entrusted every provincial matter to Pu.

sentences.zh: 太祖從容謂始興王曰：「沈璞奉時無纖介之失，在家有孝友之稱，學優才贍，文義可觀，而沈深守靜，不求名譽，甚佳。

translations.literal: Taizu at ease said to Prince of Shixing: "Shen Pu, in serving the times, has not a hair's error; at home has the reputation of filial piety and brotherly respect; learning superior, talent ample, literary meaning observable; yet deep and reserved, guarding quietude, not seeking fame and reputation— very good.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told Prince of Shixing, "Shen Pu has never faltered in office and is known at home for filial piety. He is learned, capable, and writes well, yet stays deep and quiet and does not chase reputation— excellent.

sentences.zh: 汝但應委之以事，乃宜引與晤對。

translations.literal: You need only entrust affairs to him; moreover you should invite and converse with him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Give him your business and meet with him in person.

sentences.zh: 」浚既素加賞遇，又敬奉此旨。

translations.literal: " Jun had already long added favor and treatment, and again reverently obeyed this instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Jun already valued Pu and now followed this counsel as well.

sentences.zh: 璞嘗作《舊宮賦》，久而未畢，浚與璞疏曰：「卿常有速藻，《舊宮》何其淹耶？

translations.literal: Pu once composed "Rhapsody on the Old Palace"; long yet not finished. Jun wrote to Pu: "You always have swift compositions— why is 'Old Palace' so delayed?
translations.idiomatic: Pu had begun a "Rhapsody on the Old Palace" but left it unfinished. Jun wrote, "You usually write fast— why is the 'Old Palace' piece taking so long?

sentences.zh: 想行就爾。

translations.literal: I think it is soon finished— is it?
translations.idiomatic: I expect it is nearly done.

sentences.zh: 」璞因事陳答，辭義可觀。

translations.literal: " Pu, taking occasion, submitted a reply; diction and meaning were admirable.
