translations.idiomatic: Pu answered at length; the prose was fine.

sentences.zh: 浚重教曰：「卿沈思淹日，向聊相敦問，還白斐然，遂兼紙翰。

translations.literal: Jun again instructed: "You ponder deeply for days; I just now lightly urged inquiry, yet you return with splendid whiteness and also send paper and brush writing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wrote again: "You brood for days over every line. I asked lightly and you answered at once, with a whole letter besides.

sentences.zh: 昔曹植有言，下筆成章，良謂逸才贍藻，誇其辭說，以今況之，方知其信。

translations.literal: Formerly Cao Zhi had words: 'Putting pen down, forms chapters'— truly meaning exceptional talent and ample flourish, boasting his rhetoric; comparing to today, one then knows its truth.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Zhi said he could write finished prose at a stroke. I thought that was boasting— now I see it was true.

sentences.zh: 執省躊躇，三複不已。

translations.literal: Holding and reading, hesitating; three times reviewing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: I read your words again and again and cannot put them down.

sentences.zh: 吾遠慚楚元，門盈申、白之賓，近愧梁孝，庭列枚、馬之客，欣恧交至，諒唯深矣。

translations.literal: I, far ashamed of King Yuan of Chu, whose gate was full of Shen and Bai's guests; near ashamed of Prince Xiao of Liang, whose court listed Mei and Ma's clients—joy and shame arriving together; truly only deep.
translations.idiomatic: I am shamed beside King Yuan of Chu with his guests Shen Yi and Bai Gui, and beside Prince Xiao of Liang with Mei Sheng and Ma Rong— proud and abashed at once, and deeply so.

sentences.zh: 薄因末牘，以代一面。

translations.literal: Briefly, taking this trailing document, to substitute for one meeting face to face.
translations.idiomatic: This note must stand in for a meeting.

sentences.zh: 」又與主簿顧邁、孔道存書曰：「沈璞淹思逾歲，卿研慮數旬，瑰麗之美，信同在昔。

translations.literal: " Also to Masters of Records Gu Mai and Kong Daocun a letter said: "Shen Pu's submerged thought exceeds a year; you studied intent for several tens of days— splendor and beauty, truly together in former times.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to clerks Gu Mai and Kong Daocun: "Pu brooded a year over his piece while you debated for weeks. The splendor matches the ancients.

sentences.zh: 向聊問之，而遠答累翰，辭藻豔逸，致慰良多。

translations.literal: Just now lightly asking, yet from afar answering with accumulated writings— rhetoric and flourish bright and unfettered, causing much consolation.
translations.idiomatic: I asked casually and he sent pages of bright, graceful prose— a great comfort.

sentences.zh: 既欣股肱備此髦楚，還慚予躬無德而稱。

translations.literal: Both rejoicing that arm and thigh are equipped with these outstanding talents, yet ashamed that my person has no virtue to match.
translations.idiomatic: I am glad to have such fine men at my side, yet ashamed that I have no merit to match them.

sentences.zh: 複裁少字，宣志於璞，聊因尺紙，使卿等具知厥心。

translations.literal: Again cutting a few characters, declaring intent to Pu— briefly by this foot of paper, making you all fully know his heart.
translations.idiomatic: I add a few lines for Pu so you will all know his mind.

sentences.zh: 」此書真本猶存。

translations.literal: " This letter's authentic original still exists.
translations.idiomatic: The original of this letter still survives.

sentences.zh: 浚年既長，璞固求辭事，上雖聽許，而意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Jun's years were already grown; Pu firmly requested to resign affairs. The emperor though listened and permitted, yet intent was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun came of age Pu asked to step down. The emperor consented but was displeased.

sentences.zh: 以璞為浚始興國大農，尋除秣陵令。

translations.literal: Pu was made Grand Agriculturist of Jun's Principality of Shixing; soon removed as Moling Magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was made grand agriculturist of Jun's principality, then magistrate of Moling.

sentences.zh: 時天下殷實，四方輻輳，京邑二縣，號為難治。

translations.literal: At the time all under Heaven was prosperous and solid; four directions converged like wheel spokes. The capital's two counties were called hard to govern.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was prosperous and people crowded into the capital; its two inner counties were famously hard to rule.

sentences.zh: 璞以清嚴制下，端平待物，奸吏斂手，猾民知懼。

translations.literal: Pu with pure strictness controlled subordinates, upright and level in treating things; corrupt officials withdrew hands; cunning people knew fear.
translations.idiomatic: Pu ruled subordinates with austere integrity and treated all fairly; corrupt clerks shrank back and sharp dealers learned fear.

sentences.zh: 其閭里少年，博徒酒客，或財利爭鬥，妄相誣引，前後不能判者，璞皆知其名姓，及巧詐緣由，探擿是非，各標證據，或辨甲有以知乙，或驗東而西事自顯，莫不厭伏，有如神明。

translations.literal: Youth of the lanes and quarters, gambling and wine clients, or wealth and profit disputes— falsely accusing one another, before and after unable to judge— Pu all knew their names and surnames and crafty fraud's causes, probing and picking out right and wrong, each marking evidence; or from A having [evidence] knowing B, or verifying east and west affairs self-revealed— none did not submit in satisfaction, like spirits and gods.
translations.idiomatic: When young brawlers, gamblers, and petty litigants lied about one another in cases no one could untangle, Pu knew their names and tricks, laid out the evidence, and often proved guilt from a witness on one side or a fact in another quarter until all submitted as if to a god.

sentences.zh: 以疾去職。

translations.literal: Owing to illness, left office.
translations.idiomatic: Illness forced him to resign.

sentences.zh: 太祖厚加存問，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Taizu thickly added inquiries after his welfare; rewards and gifts very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent warm inquiries and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 浚出為南徐州，謂璞曰：「浚既出蕃，卿故當臥而護之。

translations.literal: Jun went out as Southern Xuzhou and said to Pu: "Jun having gone out to a fiefdom, you therefore should lie down and yet protect it.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun went to Southern Xuzhou he told Pu, "I am leaving my fief— you must guard it even from your bed.

sentences.zh: 」與浚詔曰：「沈璞累年主簿，又經國卿，雖未嘗為行佐，今故當正參軍耶。

translations.literal: " An edict to Jun said: "Shen Pu for years was master of records, also passed through state chief clerk; though never having been traveling aide, now therefore ought he be formal aide?
translations.idiomatic: A rescript to Jun asked whether Pu, after years as chief clerk though never a traveling aide, should be made formal staff officer.

sentences.zh: 若爾，正當署餘曹，兼房任，不爾便宜行佐正署中兵，恐於選體如不多耳。

translations.literal: If so, then properly should assign remaining bureaus and concurrent inner-chamber duty; if not, then conveniently traveling aide formally appoint central military— I fear for selection form it may not be much.
translations.idiomatic: If so, give him other bureaus and household duties; if not, make him traveling aide and central military aide— though that may look thin on the appointment rolls.

sentences.zh: 」事見宋文帝中詔乃為正佐。

translations.literal: " The affair is recorded in Emperor Wen's middle edicts; thereupon [Pu] became formal aide.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is noted among Emperor Wen's mid-reign edicts; Pu was made formal aide.

sentences.zh: 俄遷宣威將軍、盱眙太守。

translations.literal: Soon moved to General Who Spreads Majesty, Xuyi Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General Who Spreads Majesty and Administrator of Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 時王師北伐，彭、汴無虞。

translations.literal: At the time the royal army marched north; Peng and Bian had no worry.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was campaigning north and the Peng and Bian region seemed secure.

sentences.zh: 璞以強寇對陣，事未可測，郡首淮隅，道當沖要，乃修城壘，浚重隍，聚材石，積鹽米，為不可勝之算。

translations.literal: Pu, with a strong enemy facing the battle line and affairs not yet measurable, the commandery head at the Huai corner, the road meeting the vital point— therefore repaired city ramparts, deepened double moats, gathered timber and stone, stored salt and rice, as calculations that could not be overcome.
translations.idiomatic: With a powerful foe across the line and Xuyi on a critical stretch of the Huai, Pu rebuilt the walls, dug moats, and stockpiled wood, stone, salt, and grain for a siege no enemy could break.

sentences.zh: 眾鹹不同，朝旨亦謂為過。

translations.literal: The crowd all differed; court intent also said it excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Others disagreed and the court thought it excessive.

sentences.zh: 俄而賊大越逸，索虜大帥托跋燾自率步騎數十萬，陵踐六州，京邑為之騷懼，百守千城，莫不奔駭。

translations.literal: Soon the bandits greatly crossed beyond; the great commander of the Suo barbarians, Tuoba Tao, personally led infantry and cavalry several hundred thousand, trampling and treading six provinces; the capital region for this was alarmed and fearful— hundred guards, thousand cities, none did not flee in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Then the enemy surged south in force: Tuoba Tao led hundreds of thousands of horsemen and footmen through six provinces, and every garrison and town panicked.

sentences.zh: 腹心勸璞還京師，璞曰：「若賊大眾，不盼小城，故無所懼。

translations.literal: Inner confidants urged Pu to return to the capital. Pu said: "If bandits are a great host, they will not regard a small city; therefore nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: His close advisers urged him to flee to the capital. Pu said, "A huge army will not bother with a small city— I am not afraid.

sentences.zh: 若肉薄來攻，則成禽也。

translations.literal: If they press flesh-close to attack, then becoming captives.
translations.idiomatic: If they come close enough to storm the walls, they become our captives.

sentences.zh: 諸軍何嘗見數十萬人聚在一處，而不敗者。

translations.literal: When have armies ever seen several hundred thousand people gathered in one place and not defeated?
translations.idiomatic: When has an army of hundreds of thousands massed in one spot without defeat?

sentences.zh: 昆陽、合淝，前事之明驗。

translations.literal: Kunyang, Hefei— former affairs' clear verification.
translations.idiomatic: Kunyang and Hefei are clear precedents.

sentences.zh: 此是吾報國之秋，諸軍封侯之日。

translations.literal: This is my season for repaying the state; the armies' day for enfeoffment as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: This is our season to serve the realm and win marquisates.

sentences.zh: 」眾既見璞神色不異，老幼在焉，人情乃定。

translations.literal: " The crowd, having seen Pu's expression unchanged and old and young present, popular sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Pu calm and families staying put, the people steadied.

sentences.zh: 收集得二千精手，謂諸將曰：「足矣。

translations.literal: Collected and obtained two thousand elite hands; said to the generals: "Enough.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered two thousand picked men and told his officers, "That is enough.

sentences.zh: 但恐賊不過爾。

translations.literal: Only fear the bandits will not come that far.
translations.idiomatic: I only fear the enemy will not come.

sentences.zh: 」賊既濟淮，諸軍將帥毛遐祚、胡崇之、臧澄之等，為虜所覆，無不殄盡，唯輔國將軍臧質挺身走，收散卒千餘人來向城。

translations.literal: " The bandits having crossed the Huai, the armies' generals Mao Xiazuo, Hu Chongzhi, Zang Chengzhi, and others were overturned by the captives— none not exterminated entirely; only Auxiliary State General Zang Zhi alone walked away, gathered scattered troops over a thousand men, and came toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy crossed the Huai, generals Mao Xiazuo, Hu Chongzhi, Zang Chengzhi, and others were wiped out; only Zang Zhi escaped with a thousand scattered troops and headed for the city.

sentences.zh: 眾謂璞曰：「若不攻則無所事眾，若其來也，城中止可容見力爾，地狹人多，鮮不為患。

translations.literal: The crowd said to Pu: "If [we] do not attack, then there is nothing to employ the crowd with. If they come, in the city only able to hold visible strength; land narrow, people many— rarely not becoming trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Some told Pu, "Without fighting we have no use for these men. If Zang Zhi enters, the city can barely hold those already here— overcrowding will bring trouble.

sentences.zh: 且敵眾我寡，人所共知，雖雲攻守不同，故當粗量強弱，知難而退，亦用兵之要。

translations.literal: Moreover enemy many, we few— what people together know. Though it is said offense and defense differ, therefore one should roughly measure strong and weak, know difficulty and withdraw— also the essential of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows we are outnumbered. Even if attack and defense differ, we should weigh the odds, retreat when we must— that too is sound generalship.

sentences.zh: 若以今眾法能退敵完城者，則全功不在我，若宜避賊歸都，會資舟楫，則更相蹂踐，正足為患。

translations.literal: If with the present host by law able to repel the enemy and complete the city, then full merit is not in us. If one should avoid bandits and return to the capital, meeting and borrowing boats— then mutually trampling, just enough to become trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If these troops could drive the enemy off, the credit would not be ours. If we flee to the capital for boats, we will trample one another and make things worse.

sentences.zh: 今閉門勿受，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Now close the gates, do not receive— is that not acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: Why not simply shut the gates and refuse them?

sentences.zh: 」璞歎曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Pu sighed: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Pu sighed. "No.

sentences.zh: 賊不能登城，為諸君保之。

translations.literal: The bandits cannot ascend the city; I guarantee it for you all.
translations.idiomatic: I promise you the enemy cannot take this wall.

sentences.zh: 舟楫之計，固已久息。

translations.literal: The plan of boats— firmly already long ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to escape by boat are long abandoned.

sentences.zh: 賊之殘害，古今之未有，屠剝之刑，眾所共見，其中有福者，不過得驅還北國作奴婢爾。

translations.literal: The bandits' cruel harm— of antiquity and today none before; flaying and stripping punishments— what the crowd together has seen. Among them the fortunate— none surpass being driven back to the northern land to become slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Their cruelty is unmatched in history; everyone has seen their butchery. The lucky ones are merely sent north as slaves.

sentences.zh: 彼雖烏合，寧不憚此耶！

translations.literal: Though they are a crow gathering, how would they not fear this!
translations.idiomatic: Even a rabble army will fear that fate.

sentences.zh: 所謂'同舟而濟，胡、越不患異心'也。

translations.literal: What is called 'same boat and cross the ford— Hu and Yue do not worry at different hearts'— that is it.
translations.idiomatic: As they say, 'Once in the same boat, even Hu and Yue do not fear divided hearts.'

sentences.zh: 今人多則退速，人少則退遲，吾寧欲專功緩賊乎！

translations.literal: Now people many, then retreat is fast; people few, then retreat is slow— would I rather want to monopolize merit and slow the bandits!
translations.idiomatic: More men make a retreat faster; fewer make it slower. Do you think I want to hoard glory and let the enemy escape?

sentences.zh: 」乃命開門納質。

translations.literal: " Thereupon ordered the gates opened to admit Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the gates opened and admitted Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質見城隍阻固，人情輯和，鮭米豐盛，器械山積，大喜，眾皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Zhi saw city moat and walls obstructed and solid, popular sentiment harmonious, grain and rice abundant, weapons piled like mountains— greatly rejoiced; the crowd all cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi found strong walls, calm people, full granaries, and arms heaped like hills. Delighted, the troops cried "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 及賊至，四面蟻集攻城，璞與質隨宜應拒，攻守三旬，殄其太半，燾乃遁走。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, on four sides like ants they gathered to attack the city. Pu and Zhi as suited resisted; offense and defense thirty days, exterminated more than half; Tao then fled and went.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy came they swarmed the walls. Pu and Zhi held for thirty days, destroyed more than half their force, and Tuoba Tao fled.

sentences.zh: 有議欲追之者，璞曰：「今兵士不多，又非素附，雖固守有餘未可以言戰也。

translations.literal: Some discussed wishing to pursue them. Pu said: "Now soldiers not many, and again not long attached; though defending firmly has surplus, one cannot yet speak of battle.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged pursuit, Pu said, "We have few troops and they are not seasoned followers. We can hold a wall but cannot yet fight in the field.

sentences.zh: 但可整舟艫，示若欲渡岸者，以速其走計，不須實行。

translations.literal: Only can ready boats and ships, show as if wishing to cross the shore— to speed their flight plan; need not actually carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Muster the boats as if we mean to cross the river— that will hurry their retreat. We need not actually go.

sentences.zh: 」鹹以為然。

translations.literal: " All approved and thought so.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 臧質以璞城主，使自上露板。

translations.literal: Zang Zhi, because Pu was city lord, had him personally submit the open report.
translations.idiomatic: Because Pu had held the city, Zang Zhi had him submit the victory report.

sentences.zh: 璞性謙虛，推功於質。

translations.literal: Pu's nature was modest and yielded merit to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Modest by nature, Pu gave the credit to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 既不自上，質露板亦不及焉。

translations.literal: Since he did not himself submit, Zhi's open report also did not reach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu did not file one himself, and Zhi's report did not mention him either.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉璞功效，遣中使深相褒美。

translations.literal: Taizu praised Pu's achievement and effect, sent a palace envoy to deeply praise and admire.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu praised Pu's achievement and sent an imperial messenger with warm commendation.

sentences.zh: 太祖又別詔曰：「近者險急，老弱殊當憂迫耶。

translations.literal: Taizu also separately decreed, saying: "Recently the danger was urgent—the old and weak especially must have been worried and pressed, yes?
translations.idiomatic: Taizu also issued a separate decree: "The recent danger must have been especially hard on the old and weak.

sentences.zh: 念卿爾時，難為心想。

translations.literal: Thinking of you at that time, it is hard to imagine your state of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of you in that hour, I can scarcely imagine your distress.

sentences.zh: 百姓流轉已還，此遣部運尋至，委卿量所贍濟也。

translations.literal: The common people who wandered have already returned; here I dispatch departmental transport soon to arrive—entrust to you to measure and provide relief.
translations.idiomatic: The displaced people are returning home. I am sending supply shipments shortly; entrust relief to your discretion.

sentences.zh: 」始興王浚亦與璞書曰：「狡虜狂凶，自送近服，偽將即斃，酋長傷殘，實天威所喪，卿諸人忠勇之效也。

translations.literal: " The Prince of Shixing Jun also wrote to Pu, saying: "The cunning barbarians, wildly fierce, themselves delivered themselves to near submission; the false general immediately perished, the chieftain wounded and maimed—truly Heaven's might caused their loss—the effect of your people's loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: " Prince Shixing also wrote Pu: "Those savage barbarians brought ruin on themselves. Their general fell at once and their chieftains were shattered—Heaven's wrath, and the fruit of your loyal courage.

sentences.zh: 吾式遏無素，致境蕪民瘠，負乘之愧，允當其責。

translations.literal: My checking and stopping without mastery caused the borderlands wasteland and the people lean—the guilt of bearing what one cannot carry—truly fitting its responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: I had no skill at defense and left the land waste and the people impoverished. The shame of an overloaded cart is mine alone.

sentences.zh: 近乞退謝愆，不蒙垂許，故以報卿。

translations.literal: Recently I begged to withdraw and apologize for faults—not granted gracious consent; therefore I use this to report to you.
translations.idiomatic: I recently asked leave to resign and acknowledge my faults, but was not permitted. I write to tell you so.

sentences.zh: 」宣城太守王僧達書與璞曰：「足下何如，想館舍正安，士馬無恙。

translations.literal: " Xuancheng Administrator Wang Sengda wrote to Pu, saying: "How are you, sir? I expect your residence is properly settled, soldiers and horses unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuancheng Administrator Wang Sengda wrote Pu: "How fare you, sir? I trust your quarters are settled and your men and horses unharmed.

sentences.zh: 離析有時，音旨無日，憂詠沈吟，增其勞望。

translations.literal: Separation and parting have their time; news and intent no day; worry and lamentation, brooding—increasing one's toil and yearning.
translations.idiomatic: Parting comes in its season, but word from you never does. My worries deepen and my longing grows.

sentences.zh: 間者獯獫扈橫，掠剝邊鄙，郵販絕塵，坰介靡達，瞻江盼淮，眇然千里。

translations.literal: Recently the Xianyun rampaged lawlessly, plundered and stripped the borderlands; postal and trade cut off all dust; no word reaches across the wilds. Gazing at the river, looking toward the Huai—a thousand li remote.
translations.idiomatic: Lately the barbarians have ravaged the borders; mail and trade have stopped. No tidings cross the wilderness, and you seem a thousand li away beyond the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 吾聞涇陽梗棘，伊滑薦遁，鳥集弦絕，患深自古。

translations.literal: I have heard of Jingyang's thorns, Yi and Hua's repeated flight, birds gathering but the bowstring broken—calamity deep since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: I know the old troubles of Jingyang and the flights across the Yi and Huai—when the string breaks amid gathering birds, disaster runs deep in history.

sentences.zh: 承知乃昔寇苦城境，勝胄朝餐，伍甲宵舍，烽鼓交警，羽鏑驟合。

translations.literal: Learning that in those days the bandits besieged the city borders—armor for morning meal, ranks of armor for night lodging; beacon drums alternating alerts, feathered bolts suddenly clashing.
translations.idiomatic: I hear how the enemy once pressed your walls—meals in armor, sleep in arms, beacon drums through the night, and arrows flying in sudden volleys.

sentences.zh: 而足下砥兵礪伍，總厲豪彥，師請一奮，氓無貳情。

translations.literal: Yet you, sir, sharpened weapons and honed ranks, gathered and urged heroic talents; the army requested one exertion—the populace without divided hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you sharpened arms and rallied your best men. One charge was all they asked, and the people stood undivided.

sentences.zh: 遂能固孤城，覆嚴對，陷死地，覿生光，古之田、孫，何以尚茲。

translations.literal: Thereby able to hold the lone city, overturn stern opposition, trapped in death ground yet showing living glory—the ancients Tian and Sun, how could they surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: You held a lone city against fierce odds and turned death ground into glory—even Tian Dan and Sun Bin could add nothing to such a deed.

sentences.zh: 商驛始通，粗知梗概，崇贊膽智，嘉賀文猛，甚善甚善。

translations.literal: Merchant couriers just opened; roughly know the outline; I honor and praise your courage and wisdom, rejoice and celebrate your literary and martial fierceness—very good, very good.
translations.idiomatic: Now that merchants' couriers have resumed, I have heard the outline. I praise your courage and wit and rejoice in your literary and martial prowess. Excellent—excellent!

sentences.zh: 吾近以戎暴橫斥，規效情命，收龜落簪，星舍京里，既獲遄至，胡馬卷跡，支離沾德，複繼前緒，《行葦》之歡，實協初慮。

translations.literal: I recently because of barbarian violence was driven out, planned to offer my feelings and life, gathered tortoise and let fall the hairpin, by starlight left the capital; having obtained swift arrival, Hu horses rolled away their tracks; the scattered received virtue and continued the former thread—the joy of "Traveling Rushes," truly matching my initial thought.
translations.idiomatic: I was lately driven from the capital by barbarian fury and barely escaped with my life. Once I reached safety the Hu horsemen vanished; refugees found mercy, and the old order resumed. The joy of the "Traveling Rushes" poem indeed fulfilled my first hope.

sentences.zh: 但乖塗重隔，顧增慨涕，比恆疾臥，憂委兼疊，裁書送想，無斁久懷。」

translations.literal: But separated ways heavily blocked, looking back increases sighing tears; recently always ill abed, worries and commissions piled together; I cut this letter to send my thoughts—may it not weary my long-held feelings."
translations.idiomatic: Yet our paths lie far apart and sorrow comes unbidden. I have been ill and burdened with care. This letter sends my thoughts; may it not fail my long devotion."

sentences.zh: 征還，淮南太守，賞賜豐厚，日夕宴見。

translations.literal: Summoned back, Huainan Administrator; rewards and gifts abundant; day and night feasted and received audience.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made Administrator of Huainan, richly rewarded, and feasted and received in audience day after day.

sentences.zh: 朝士有言璞功者，上曰：「臧質姻戚，又年位在前，盱眙元功，當以歸之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen who spoke of Pu's merit—the Emperor said: "Zang Zhi is a marriage relative, and again age and rank are ahead; the chief merit of Xuyi should be returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: When courtiers praised Pu's merit, the Emperor said, "Zang Zhi is a kinsman by marriage and senior in years and rank. The chief credit for Xuyi belongs to him.

sentences.zh: 沈璞每以謙自牧，唯恐賞之居前，此士燮之意也。

translations.literal: Shen Pu always with humility cultivated himself, only feared rewards placing Zhi ahead—this is Shi Xie's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Pu was ever modest and feared any reward that put Zhi first—the spirit of Shi Xie.

sentences.zh: 」時中書郎缺，尚書令何尚之領吏部，舉璞及謝莊、陸展，事不行。

translations.literal: " At that time the Central Secretariat Attendant post was vacant; Minister of Works He Shangzhi headed the Personnel Bureau, recommended Pu together with Xie Zhuang and Lu Zhan—the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the post of Central Secretariat Attendant was vacant. Minister He Shangzhi, heading the Personnel Bureau, recommended Pu along with Xie Zhuang and Lu Zhan, but the appointment did not go through.

sentences.zh: 事見文帝中詔。

translations.literal: The matter is seen in Emperor Wen's palace decrees.
translations.idiomatic: The affair is recorded in Emperor Wen's palace decrees.

sentences.zh: 凡中詔今悉在台，猶法書典書也。

translations.literal: All palace decrees now are entirely at the Secretariat—like legal documents and archival documents.
translations.idiomatic: All such palace decrees are now kept at the Secretariat, like formal legal archives.

sentences.zh: 三十年，元兇弑立，璞乃號泣曰：「一門蒙殊常之恩，而逢若斯之運，悠悠上天，此何人哉！

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the chief villain murdered and established himself. Pu then wailed, saying: "One household received extraordinary grace, yet encountered such a fate—vast, vast Heaven, what sort of person is this!
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the usurper seized the throne by murder. Pu wept and said, "Our house owed extraordinary grace, yet met such a fate—O Heaven above, what man is this!

sentences.zh: 」日夜憂歎，以至動疾。

translations.literal: " Day and night worry and sigh, until it reached stirring illness.
translations.idiomatic: " He grieved day and night until illness took hold.

sentences.zh: 會二凶逼令送老弱還都，璞性篤孝，尋聞尊老應幽執，輒哽咽不自勝，疾遂增篤，不堪遠迎，世祖義軍至界首，方得致身。

translations.literal: It happened that the two villains forced an order to send the old and weak back to the capital. Pu's nature was deeply filial; soon hearing his honored elder should be secretly imprisoned, immediately choked with sobs beyond control. Illness then increased severe; unable to bear going far to welcome—when Emperor Xiaowu's righteous army reached the border, only then able to offer himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the two usurpers ordered the old and weak sent back to the capital, the devoted Pu learned his father would be imprisoned. He broke down sobbing and grew gravely ill. Too sick to go far to meet the Emperor's forces, he was only able to present himself when they reached the border.

sentences.zh: 先是，琅邪顏竣欲與璞交，不酬其意，竣以致恨。

translations.literal: Before this, Langya Yan Jun wished to befriend Pu; he did not answer his intent—Jun therefore bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan Jun of Langya had sought friendship with Pu, who declined. Jun hence bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及世祖將至都，方有讒說以璞奉迎之晚，橫罹世難，時年三十八。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu was about to reach the capital, then there were slanderous words saying Pu welcomed him late—he was cut off by worldly calamity. At the time, age thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Xiaowu neared the capital, slanders arose that Pu had delayed in welcoming him. He perished in the turmoil. He was thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 所著賦、頌、贊、祭文、誄、七、吊、四五言詩、箋、表，皆遇亂零失，今所餘詩筆雜文凡二十首。

translations.literal: His compositions—fu, eulogy, praise, sacrificial text, dirge, "seven," lament, four- and five-character poems, letters, memorials—all met disorder and were scattered and lost; what remains of poetry, brushwork, and mixed essays totals twenty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: His fu, eulogies, praises, sacrificial writings, dirges, "seven" pieces, laments, four- and five-character poems, letters, and memorials were all lost in the turmoil. Twenty mixed poems and essays survive.

sentences.zh: 璞有子曰囗。

translations.literal: Pu had a son named [missing character].
translations.idiomatic: Pu had a son whose name is lost.

sentences.zh: 伯玉，字德潤，虔子子也。

translations.literal: Boyu, style Derun—the son of Qian's son.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu, style name Derun, was the son of Shen Qian's son.

sentences.zh: 溫恭有行業，能為文章。

translations.literal: Gentle and respectful with conduct and accomplishment; able to compose literary works.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle, respectful, and accomplished, he could write well.

sentences.zh: 少除世祖武陵國侍郎，轉右常侍，南中郎行參軍，自國入府，以文義見知，文章多見世祖集。

translations.literal: In youth appointed Prince of Wuling Attendant for Emperor Xiaowu, transferred to Right Regular Attendant, Southern General of the Guard Acting Adjutant; from the principality into the palace, by literary learning known; his essays mostly appear in Emperor Xiaowu's collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Young he served as Attendant in Emperor Xiaowu's Principality of Wuling, then Right Regular Attendant and Acting Adjutant under the Southern General of the Guard. Moving from principality to palace staff, he won notice for letters and learning; many of his pieces appear in the Emperor's collected writings.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，除員外散騎郎，不拜。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant—did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, he was made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 左衛顏竣請為司馬。

translations.literal: Left Guard Yan Jun requested him as Army Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jun of the Left Guard asked to have him as Marshal.

sentences.zh: 出補句容令，在縣有能名。

translations.literal: Went out and filled the post of Jurong Magistrate; in the county had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: He went out to serve as magistrate of Jurong, where he earned a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 複為江夏王義恭太宰行參軍，與奉朝請謝超宗、何法盛校書東宮，復為餘姚令，還為衛尉丞。

translations.literal: Again served as Acting Adjutant to Grand Preceptor of Prince Jiangxia Yigong; together with Gentleman-at-Court Xie Chaozong and He Fasheng collated books in the Eastern Palace; again served as Yuyao Magistrate; returned as Aide of the Minister of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He became Acting Adjutant to Grand Preceptor Yigong of Jiangxia, and with Xie Chaozong and He Fasheng collated texts in the Eastern Palace. He served again as magistrate of Yuyao, then returned as Aide in the Ministry of Guards.

sentences.zh: 世祖舊臣故佐，普皆升顯，伯玉自守私門，朔望未嘗問訊。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's old ministers and former aides—all generally were promoted and exalted. Boyu kept to his private gate; on new and full moon never inquired after them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's former aides were all promoted, but Boyu kept to his home and never visited them even on the first and fifteenth of the month.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯、戴法興等並有蕃邸之舊，一不造問，由是官次不進。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo, Dai Faxing, and others all had old ties in the princely residence—he never once paid visits; hence official rank did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shibo, Dai Faxing, and others had old ties at the princely residence, yet he never called on any of them. His rank therefore stalled.

sentences.zh: 上以伯玉容狀似畫圖仲尼像，常呼為孔丘。

translations.literal: The Emperor because Boyu's appearance resembled the painted image of Zhongni, often called him Kong Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thought Boyu looked like a painted portrait of Confucius and often called him Kong Qiu.

sentences.zh: 舊制，車駕出行，衛尉丞直門，常戎服。

translations.literal: Under old regulations, when the imperial carriage went out, the Minister of Guards aide on gate duty—usually in military garb.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule, when the Emperor went abroad the Guards aide at the gate wore military dress.

sentences.zh: 張永謂伯玉曰：「此職乖卿志。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong said to Boyu: "This post goes against your aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong told Boyu, "This duty ill suits your bent.

sentences.zh: 」王景文亦與伯玉有舊，常陪輦出，指伯玉白上：「孔丘奇形容。

translations.literal: " Wang Jingwen also had old ties with Boyu; often accompanied the carriage out, pointed at Boyu and told the Emperor: "Kong Qiu's wondrous appearance.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Jingwen, who also knew Boyu well, often rode out with the Emperor, pointed to Boyu, and said, "Kong Qiu has a remarkable face.

sentences.zh: 」上於是特聽伯玉直門服玄衣。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon specially permitted Boyu on gate duty to wear dark robes.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then specially allowed Boyu to wear dark robes at the gate.

sentences.zh: 出為晉安王子勳前軍行參軍，侍子勳讀書。

translations.literal: Went out as Acting Adjutant of the Vanguard under Prince Jin'an Zixun; attended Zixun's reading.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Acting Adjutant on Prince Zixun of Jin'an's vanguard staff and tutored the prince in his studies.

sentences.zh: 隨府轉鎮軍行佐。

translations.literal: Following the headquarters, transferred to Acting Assistant of the Garrison General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the headquarters and became Acting Assistant to the Garrison General.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝時，王景文領選，謂子勳典簽沈光祖曰：「鄧琬一旦為長史行事，沈伯玉先帝在蕃囗佐，今猶不改，民生定不應佳。

translations.literal: During the Former Deposed Emperor's time, Wang Jingwen headed selection and told Zixun's Chief Clerk Shen Guangzu: "If Deng Wan suddenly acts as Chief Administrator, Shen Boyu—the Former Emperor's princely residence [missing character] aide—still has not changed, the people's livelihood surely ought not to be good.
translations.idiomatic: During the Former Deposed Emperor's reign, Wang Jingwen headed selection and told Zixun's Chief Clerk Shen Guangzu, "If Deng Wan suddenly takes charge as Chief Administrator, Shen Boyu—once an aide in the late Emperor's princely household—still has not changed his ways, the people's welfare surely will not be well served.

sentences.zh: 」戴法興聞景文此言，乃轉伯玉為參軍事。

translations.literal: " Dai Faxing heard Jingwen's these words; thereupon transferred Boyu to Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: " Hearing this, Dai Faxing transferred Boyu to a staff officer's post.

sentences.zh: 子勳初起兵，轉府功曹。

translations.literal: When Zixun first raised troops, transferred to Headquarters Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun first rebelled, Boyu became Merit Officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 及即偽位，以為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When he then assumed the false throne, made him Central Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zixun claimed the throne, he was made Central Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，伯玉為衛尉丞，太宗為衛尉，共事甚美。

translations.literal: Initially, Boyu was Guards Aide; Emperor Ming was Minister of Guards—serving together very well.
translations.idiomatic: At first Boyu was Guards Aide while Emperor Ming headed the Ministry of Guards; they worked together admirably.

sentences.zh: 及子勳敗，伯玉下獄，見原，猶以在南無誠，被責，除南台御史，尋轉武陵國詹事，又轉大農，母老解職。

translations.literal: When Zixun was defeated, Boyu was imprisoned, received pardon, yet because in the south he lacked sincerity was blamed; appointed Southern Secretariat Censor; soon transferred to Prince of Wuling Chamberlain; again transferred to Grand Agriculture; mother old—resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: After Zixun's defeat Boyu was imprisoned and pardoned, but was censured for lack of loyalty in the south. He was made Censor of the Southern Secretariat, then Chamberlain of Wuling, then Grand Agriculture Officer. He resigned when his mother grew old.

sentences.zh: 貧薄理盡，閑臥一室，自非吊省親舊，不嘗出門。

translations.literal: Poor and thin, resources exhausted; idly lay in one room—unless mourning visits or calling on old friends, never went out the door.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and with nothing left, he lay idle in one room and rarely left it except to mourn or visit old friends.

sentences.zh: 司徒袁粲、司空褚淵深相知賞，選為永世令，轉在永興，皆有能名。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Yuan Can and Minister of Works Chu Yuan deeply knew and appreciated him; selected as Yongshi Magistrate; transferred to Yongxing—both had reputations for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can, Minister over the Masses, and Chu Yuan, Minister of Works, admired him deeply. He was chosen magistrate of Yongshi and then Yongxing, earning a name for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽三年，卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: Later Deposed Emperor, third year of Yuanhui—died; at the time age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Yuanhui under the Later Deposed Emperor, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 伯玉性至孝，奉親有聞，未嘗妄取於人，有物輒散之知故。

translations.literal: Boyu's nature was utmost filial; serving parents had renown; never rashly took from others; when he had things, immediately dispersed them to acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu was deeply filial and famed for honoring his parents. He never took what was not his and gave whatever he had to friends.

sentences.zh: 溫雅有風味，和而能辨，與人共事，皆為深交。

translations.literal: Gentle and refined with flavor; harmonious yet able to discern; with people serving together—all became deep friendships.
translations.idiomatic: Graceful and discerning, harmonious yet firm, he made close friends of all who worked with him.

sentences.zh: 弟仲玉，泰始末，為甯朔長史、蜀郡太守。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhongyu—at the end of Taishi, served as Chief Administrator of Ningsuo and Administrator of Shujun.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhongyu, late in the Taishi era, was Chief Administrator of Ningsuo and Administrator of Shu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史劉亮卒，仲玉行府州事。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Liu Liang died; Zhongyu acted in prefecture and province affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Liu Liang of Yizhou died, Zhongyu governed the prefecture and province.

sentences.zh: 巴西李承明為亂，仲玉遣司馬王天生討平之。

translations.literal: Li Chengming of Baxi raised disorder; Zhongyu dispatched Army Marshal Wang Tiansheng to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chengming rebelled in Baxi, Zhongyu sent Marshal Wang Tiansheng to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 廢帝詔以為安成王撫軍中兵參軍，加建威將軍。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor decreed to appoint him Central Army Adjutant under the Pacifying General for Prince Ancheng; additionally General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor appointed him Central Army Adjutant under Prince Ancheng's Pacifying General and made him General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之請為征西諮議，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi requested him as Western Campaign Adviser—did not accept appointment; died.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi asked to have him as Western Campaign Adviser, but before he could accept the post he died.

sentences.zh: 史臣年十三而孤，少頗好學，雖棄日無功，而伏膺不改。

translations.literal: The historian was orphaned at age thirteen; in youth rather fond of learning; though days wasted without achievement, yet embraced it without change.
translations.idiomatic: The historian was orphaned at thirteen. Though studious from youth, years passed with little to show—yet he never abandoned his commitment.

sentences.zh: 常以晉氏一代，竟無全書，年二十許，便有撰述之意。

translations.literal: He always considered the Jin dynasty one generation—ultimately no complete book; at age about twenty, then had the intent to compile and narrate.
translations.idiomatic: He felt that the Jin dynasty lacked a complete history, and by about twenty he intended to write one.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，征西將軍蔡興宗為啟明帝，有敕賜許，自此迄今，年逾二十，所撰之書，凡一百二十卷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Western Campaign General Cai Xingzong memorialized to Emperor Ming; there was a decree granting permission. From then until now, years exceeding twenty; the book compiled—altogether one hundred twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taishi, General Cai Xingzong asked Emperor Ming, who granted permission. More than twenty years have passed since, and his work totals one hundred twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 條流雖舉，而采掇未周，永明初，遇盜失第五帙。

translations.literal: Categories and streams though set forth, yet collection and gathering not complete; at the beginning of Yongming, met bandits and lost the fifth fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Though the outline was complete, materials were still lacking. Early in Yongming a theft cost him the fifth fascicle.

sentences.zh: 建元四年未終，被敕撰國史。

translations.literal: Before the fourth year of Jianyuan ended, received decree to compile national history.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fourth year of Jianyuan ended, he was ordered to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，又朅奏兼著作郎，撰次起居注。

translations.literal: Yongming year two—again submitted memorial concurrently as Compiler; compiled and ordered the Diaries of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was additionally appointed Compiler and took charge of the court diaries.

sentences.zh: 自茲王役，無暇搜撰。

translations.literal: From this royal service, no leisure to search and compile.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial duties since then left him no time for research and writing.

sentences.zh: 五年春，又被敕撰《宋書》。

translations.literal: Fifth year spring—again received decree to compile the Book of Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was again ordered to compile the Book of Song.

sentences.zh: 六年二月畢功，表上之，曰：

translations.literal: Sixth year second month—work completed; submitted memorial presenting it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year the work was finished. He memorialized the throne, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣約言：臣聞大禹刊木，事炳虞書，西伯戡黎，功煥商典。

translations.literal: Your subject Yue says: Your subject has heard that Da Yu marked trees—the matter shines in the Yu documents; the Western Duke subdued Li—the merit glorifies the Shang canon.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Yue reports: I have read that Yu the Great marked the trees, memorialized in the Documents of Yu, and that the Western Duke subdued the Li people, his merit recorded in the Shang canons.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇基積峻，帝烈弘深，樹德往朝，立勳前代，若不觀風唐世，無以見帝媯之美，自非睹亂秦餘，何用知漢祖之業。

translations.literal: Prostrate considering—the imperial foundation accumulated lofty, imperial achievement vast and deep; planted virtue in former courts, established merit in former ages—if one does not observe customs in the Tang age, there is no means to see Emperor Gui's beauty; if not oneself seeing chaos in Qin remnants, what use to know Han Founder's enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Your imperial foundation rises high and your achievements run deep; virtue planted in past reigns and merit won in former ages. Without studying the ways of Tang, one cannot grasp Yao's glory; without witnessing the ruin after Qin, one cannot understand the Han founder's rise.

sentences.zh: 是以掌言未記，爰動天情，曲詔史官，追述大典。

translations.literal: Therefore the records unwritten moved Heaven's feeling; indirectly decreed the historiographers to pursue and narrate the great canon.
translations.idiomatic: Because the record was lacking, Your Majesty moved to act. You graciously commanded the historiographers to compile the great chronicle.

sentences.zh: 臣實庸妄，文史多闕，以茲不才。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly mediocre and reckless; literary and historical knowledge many gaps—with this lack of talent.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy and ill versed in letters and history—a man of scant talent.

sentences.zh: 對揚盛旨，是用夕惕載懷，忘其寢食者也。

translations.literal: Responding to and spreading the august intent—therefore evening vigil fills the breast, forgetting sleep and food.
translations.idiomatic: Facing Your lofty charge, I have worked day and night and forgotten sleep and food.

sentences.zh: 臣約頓首死罪：竊惟宋氏南面，承曆統天，雖世窮八主，年減百載，而兵車亟動，國道屢屯，垂文簡牘，事數繁廣。

translations.literal: Your subject Yue prostrate, death crime: I privately consider the Song clan facing south, receiving the calendar and uniting Heaven—though generations exhausted eight rulers, years reduced from a full century, yet chariots and arms repeatedly moved, the state's path repeatedly troubled; hanging texts on bamboo slips—affairs numerous and vast.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Yue, prostrate and deserving death: The Song faced south and held the mandate, though eight rulers reigned in less than a century. Armies marched repeatedly and the realm knew constant distress. The written record is vast and the affairs numberless.

sentences.zh: 若夫英主啟基，名臣建績，拯世夷難之功，配天光宅之運，亦足以勒銘鐘鼎，昭被方策。

translations.literal: As for enlightened rulers founding the base, famed ministers establishing merit—saving the age and leveling difficulty's merit, matching Heaven and dwelling in glory's fortune—also sufficient to inscribe bells and cauldrons, illumined and spread in regional annals.
translations.idiomatic: Its enlightened founders and great ministers who saved the realm and matched Heaven's favor deserve inscription on bells and tripods and a place in the annals.

sentences.zh: 及虐後暴朝，前王罕二，國釁家禍，曠古未書，又可以式規萬葉，作鑒於後。

translations.literal: And cruel successors, violent courts—former kings rarely matched in pairs; national calamity and family disaster, unmatched in antiquity in writing—also can serve as model for ten thousand generations, making a mirror for those after.
translations.idiomatic: Its cruel successors and tyrannical reigns, dynastic ruin and familial disaster rarely paralleled in history, likewise offer lessons for all ages and a mirror for posterity.

sentences.zh: 宋故著作郎何承天始撰《宋書》，草立紀傳，止于武帝功臣，篇牘未廣。

translations.literal: Former Song Compiler He Chengtian first compiled the Book of Song; drafted and established annals and biographies, stopping at Emperor Wu's meritorious ministers—documents not extensive.
translations.idiomatic: The late Compiler He Chengtian first began the Book of Song, drafting annals and biographies only as far as Emperor Wu's meritorious ministers—the work remained incomplete.

sentences.zh: 其所撰志，唯《天文》、《律曆》，自此外，悉委奉朝請山謙之。

translations.literal: The treatises he compiled—only "Astronomy" and "Calendars and Chronology"; apart from these, all entrusted to Gentleman-at-Court Shan Qianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Of the treatises he wrote only Astronomy and Calendars and Chronology survive; the rest he entrusted to Shan Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 謙之，孝建初，又被詔撰述，尋值病亡，仍使南台侍御史蘇寶生續造諸傳，元嘉名臣，皆其所撰。

translations.literal: Qianzhi—in the beginning of Xiaojian, again received decree to compile; soon met illness and death; still had Southern Secretariat Attending Censor Su Baosheng continue crafting the various biographies; Yuanjia famed ministers—all compiled by him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Qianzhi was again ordered to continue in early Xiaojian but soon died. Attending Censor Su Baosheng of the Southern Secretariat then wrote the biographies, including all the famed ministers of the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 寶生被誅，大明中，又命著作郎徐爰踵成前作。

translations.literal: Baosheng was executed; in the Daming era, again ordered Compiler Xu Ai to follow and complete the former work.
translations.idiomatic: After Baosheng was executed, in the Daming era Compiler Xu Ai was ordered to finish the earlier work.

sentences.zh: 爰因何、蘇所述，勒為一史，起自義熙之初，訖於大明之末。

translations.literal: Ai based on what He and Su narrated, compiled into one history—beginning from the start of Yixi, ending at the end of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai combined the work of He and Su into one history from the start of Yixi to the end of Daming.

sentences.zh: 至於臧質、魯爽、王僧達諸傳，又皆孝武所造。

translations.literal: As for the biographies of Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, Wang Sengda and others—all again were made by Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, Wang Sengda, and others were all written by Emperor Xiaowu himself.

sentences.zh: 自永光以來，至於禪讓，十餘年內，闕而不續，一代典文，始末未舉。

translations.literal: From Yongguang onward to the abdication—within ten-odd years, gaps and no continuation; one generation's canonical texts, beginning and end not fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yongguang era to the abdication—more than ten years—the record was left unfinished, and that generation's full story was never told.

sentences.zh: 且事屬當時，多非實錄，又立傳之方，取捨乖衷，進由時旨，退傍世情，垂之方來，難以取信。

translations.literal: Moreover affairs belong to the present time—many not true records; also the method of establishing biographies—selection and rejection against the center; advancing by current intent, retreating beside worldly sentiment—hanging for the future, hard to obtain trust.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover much that concerns recent times is not faithful record. Biographies were chosen to suit the moment and popular sentiment rather than truth, and cannot be trusted by posterity.

sentences.zh: 臣以謹更創立，製成新史，始自義熙肇號，終於升明三年。

translations.literal: Your subject therefore respectfully renewed and established, made into new history—beginning from Yixi first era name, ending at the third year of Shengming.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore carefully created a new history from the first Yixi era year to the third year of Shengming.

sentences.zh: 桓玄、譙縱、盧循、馬、魯之徒，身為晉賊，非關後代。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan, Qiao Zong, Lu Xun, Ma, Lu and such ilk—bodies as Jin bandits, not related to the later dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan, Qiao Zong, Lu Xun, Ma, and Lu were enemies of Jin, not figures for the later dynasty's history.

sentences.zh: 吳隱、謝混、郗僧施，義止前朝，不宜濫入宋典。

translations.literal: Wu Yin, Xie Hun, Xi Sengshi—righteousness stops at the former dynasty; ought not rashly enter Song canon.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yin, Xie Hun, and Xi Sengshi belong to the previous dynasty and should not be included in the Song annals.

sentences.zh: 劉毅、何無忌、魏詠之、檀恁之、孟昶、諸葛長民，志在興複，情非造宋，今並刊除，歸之晉籍。

translations.literal: Liu Yi, He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, Tan Qinzhi, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin—will aimed at restoring [Jin], feeling not toward creating Song; now all excised and removed, returned to Jin registers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, Tan Qinzhi, Meng Chang, and Zhuge Changmin sought to restore Jin, not to found Song. I have removed them and assigned them to the Jin record.

sentences.zh: 臣遠愧南、董，近謝遷、固，以閭閻小才，述一代盛典，屬辭比事，望古慚良，鞠躬跼蹐，靦汗亡厝。

translations.literal: Your subject far ashamed before Nan and Dong, near yielding to Qian and Gu—with alleyway petty talent, narrating one generation's great ceremony—arranging words and comparing affairs, looking to antiquity ashamed at the good, bowing body cramped and constrained, ashamed sweat with no place to set.
translations.idiomatic: I am far unworthy of Nan Shi and Dong Hu, and no match even for Sima Qian and Ban Gu. A man of small talent from humble streets, I narrate a generation's grand chronicle. Comparing my words to the ancients, I bow in shame and know not where to hide my face.

sentences.zh: 本紀列傳，繕寫已畢，合志表七十卷，臣今謹奏呈。

translations.literal: Basic annals and biographies—copying already completed; together with treatises and tables seventy juan—your subject now respectfully memorializes and presents.
translations.idiomatic: The annals and biographies are copied and complete—seventy juan including treatises and tables. I respectfully present them now.

sentences.zh: 所撰諸志，須成續上。

translations.literal: The various treatises compiled—when complete will continue to be submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The treatises I have written will be submitted when finished.

sentences.zh: 謹條目錄，詣省拜表奉書以聞。

translations.literal: Respectfully itemize the catalog; go to the Secretariat, bow in memorial and present the book to report.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully append the table of contents and submit this memorial and text for Your Majesty's notice.

sentences.zh: 臣約誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首！

translations.literal: Your subject Yue truly fearful truly trembling—prostrate prostrate!
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Yue, in deepest fear and trembling, prostrates himself!

sentences.zh: 死罪死罪！

translations.literal: Death crime death crime!
translations.idiomatic: Deserving death, deserving death!
